message.content:
In the repo /home/nick/work/andesim (branch llamacpp), the docs/ files are deleted in the working tree but still tracked in git. Use `git show HEAD:<path>` to read them.

Audit the DOCUMENTATION for a first-time external user who receives a release package of "AndeSim" (an Andes RISC-V hybrid simulator: QEMU functional + vsim cycle-accurate, sharing state). Be thorough.

Report:
1. For each tracked doc (docs/USER_GUIDE.md, docs/FRS.md, docs/MRD.md, docs/profile.md, docs/engine_interface.md, docs/switching_modes_tutorial.md, docs/llama_roi_howto.md, docs/hybrid_state_transport_problems.md, docs/csr_transport_ROADMAP.md, docs/hybrid_marker_quickstart.ipynb, and root README.md, ROADMAP*.md, REFACTOR_ROADMAP.md): its size in lines, its intended audience, and whether it is user-facing product doc vs internal dev/roadmap notes.
2. Read README.md and docs/USER_GUIDE.md fully. Summarize what an installation + first-run flow looks like today. Identify concrete gaps: steps that assume the author's own machine (hardcoded paths like /home/nick, internal hostnames, internal repo URLs), missing prerequisites, undocumented flags.
3. Grep the WHOLE repo (all tracked files, including scripts, src, tests) for hardcoded absolute paths (/home/nick, /home/*), internal hostnames or IPs, internal URL/domains (gitea, jenkins, andestech internal hosts), and any credentials/tokens. List each with file:line. This matters because they leak into a release.
4. Does any doc explain what a user must provide themselves (QEMU build, vsim build, RISC-V toolchain) vs what ships?
5. Is there any doc describing supported engines/models and how a user picks one (`./andesim list models|engines`)?

Return an organized factual report with file:line references. Do not edit anything.

attachment.content:
- cc-log: Lightweight system log to record all Claude Code behavior (tool use, subagent creation, compaction, permissions, session lifecycle) for analysis. Use when the user wants to enable/disable behavior logging, analyze Claude Code session logs, list saved logs, or understand Claude Code's tool usage patterns. Trigger on: "cc-log", "behavior log", "system log", "record behavior", "log enable", "log disable", "analyze log".
- domain-modeling: Build and sharpen a project's domain model. Use when discussing codebase terminology, writing or editing a CONTEXT.md, or recording or editing an ADR.
- grilling: Grill the user relentlessly about a plan, decision, or idea. Use when the user wants to stress-test their thinking, or uses any 'grill' trigger phrases.
- iree-optimizer: Agentic per-dispatch tile-size tuner for IREE CPU codegen on RISC-V. Keeps IREE's chosen pipeline (CPUDoubleTilingExpert / CPUConvTileAndDecomposeExpert / CPUBufferOpsTileAndVectorize) and only overrides the root linalg op's lowering_config<tile_sizes = [...]>. Each round reads the best-so-far RISC-V assembly (LMUL, VLmax, register spills) to ground the next tile-size proposal; pre-compile divisibility gate ensures tiles divide their parent extents (no tail loop); a post-compile check of the IR after iree-codegen-generic-vectorization confirms no tail/masked main path. Compiles via iree_tuner.py, benchmarks on FPGA, iterates. Use whenever the user mentions tuning IREE dispatch tile sizes, agentic tile search, or wants to replace GA-based tile-size search with LLM-driven search. Trigger on "iree optimize", "optimize dispatch", "tile tune", or references to dispatch .mlir files for performance tuning.
- libnn-optimizer: Autonomous optimization workflow for libnn RISC-V neural network library functions
in the agentic_libnn_opt project. Use this skill when the user wants to optimize a
libnn function for FPGA performance, run the libnn optimization loop, validate the
optimization config, parse FPGA hardware features, extract shapes from perf test files,
or manage the optimization state machine. Trigger when: user mentions "optimize",
"libnn", "FPGA perf", "optimization loop", "validate config",
"phase gather/baseline/iterate/evaluate", "perf test", or references opt/config.toml,
opt/state.json, or any libnn function optimization task.
- libnn-wiki-writer: Internal style guide for writing docs/wiki/ pages during /libnn-optimizer learn phase. Not a standalone skill -- read by the optimize agent.
- mlir-transform-writer: Write MLIR transform dialect scripts that directly control IR lowering - tiling, fusion, vectorization, bufferization, GPU thread mapping, shared memory promotion, and more. Use this skill whenever someone asks to generate, write, or modify a transform dialect script, transform library, codegen strategy, or tuning spec in MLIR. Also trigger when the request involves composing IR transformations for linalg ops, controlling IREE codegen pipelines via transform dialect, or replacing annotation-only configs with full transform strategies. Covers both upstream MLIR transform ops and IREE-specific extensions.
- skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- spec-human: Create a human-reviewable architecture spec using a 6-section template (Summary, Background, Architecture, Interface, Edge Cases, Alternatives) BEFORE implementing a non-trivial design. Triggered explicitly via /spec-human <topic>, or when the user says "write a human spec", "create a review-ready design doc", "spec this out for review", or "I need a spec for X before we build it". Produces an ASCII markdown document at ./specs/<slug>.md aimed at peer engineers and tech leads who need to validate core architecture and trade-offs in 5 minutes. Do NOT auto-trigger on general design questions or coding tasks - this is a deliberate review gate that only fires on explicit request. For LLM-targeted specs (future sibling skill), use /spec-llm instead.
- ralph-loop:cancel-ralph: Cancel active Ralph Loop
- ralph-loop:help: Explain Ralph Loop plugin and available commands
- ralph-loop:ralph-loop: Start Ralph Loop in current session
- design: Create a design canvas - a multi-artboard visual design published as an Artifact that runs Claude Design's canvas editor (an early preview of Claude Design inside Claude Code). You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces - posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Use when someone wants a design, mockup, wireframe, UI or screen design, landing page, poster, flyer, brochure, banner, card, one-pager, or any visual layout they would rather tweak by hand than in code. Only for CREATING or re-seeding a canvas; an existing one is edited in its published Artifact.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including a skill-instructed Markdown one - Markdown is never a shortcut past the design pass.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts - when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, remembering what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — it saves new versions of itself), keeping state shared across viewers, knowing who is viewing, asking Claude a question of its own, storing files people add, or handing the viewer a file to save. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- workflow-authoring: Reference for writing a Workflow tool script (script API and gotchas, resume, quality patterns, worked examples). Load before authoring a script for a workflow the user already opted into; it does not itself authorize running one.
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

1 # hybrid_sim
   2 
   3 Workspace for the Andes hybrid simulator: QEMU 9.x (functional, MHz) + vsim
   4 (SystemC + Verilator, cycle-accurate) sharing memory and architectural state
   5 across a magic-CSR boundary.
   6 
   7 Submodule:
   8 
   9 - `include/` - the shared ABI (`andesim_abi` repo): the `hybrid_state_v1` wire
  10   contract under `include/hybrid/`, shared by the plugin, the driver, and vsim.
  11 
  12 QEMU and vsim are integrated as prebuilt external binaries (set `QEMU_BIN_DIR` and
  13 `VSIM_BIN_DIR` in `config.env`; see `config.env.example`), not vendored as
  14 submodules. vsim sources live in the separate `hybrid_vsim` repo, built there.
  15 
  16 ## Quickstart
  17 
  18 ```sh
  19 git clone --recursive https://gitea.andestech.com/nick/hybrid_sim && cd hybrid_sim
  20 bash scripts/build_all.sh
  21 bash scripts/test_all.sh
  22 ```
  23 
  24 Subcommands: `run`, `profile`, `list`, `doctor`. Run `./andesim -h` for the
  25 full list. `docs/USER_GUIDE.md` is the end-user guide: first runs on
  26 each model, then every `run` option one by one.
  27 `./andesim run --mode hybrid --print-memmap --engine <id>` prints the
  28 hybrid-supported guest memory map (USER_GUIDE section 5.5).
  29 
  30 ## Host dependencies
  31 
  32 - C/C++ toolchain (clang preferred), CMake >= 3.20, ninja
  33 - Python 3
  34 - glib-2.0 dev (for the QEMU plugin)
  35 - pkg-config
  36 - a prebuilt `qemu-system-riscv64` (external; this repo no longer builds QEMU --
  37   set `QEMU_BIN_DIR` in `config.env`)
  38 - a prebuilt vsim (external; this repo no longer builds vsim -- set `VSIM_BIN_DIR`
  39   in `config.env` to your vsim checkout's `build/` dir)
  40 
  41 ## Outputs
  42 
  43 After `bash scripts/build_all.sh`:
  44 
  45 - `qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so` (+ `libhotIterationLoop.so`, the `andesim profile` plugin)
  46 
  47 QEMU and vsim are external prebuilt binaries: `$QEMU_BIN_DIR/qemu-system-riscv64`
  48 and `$VSIM_BIN_DIR/sim_*` (set both in `config.env`).

1 # andesim User Guide
   2 
   3 Audience: an engineer who wants to RUN programs on the Andes simulators
   4 through `./andesim` and measure cycle counts. This guide covers every
   5 user-facing option and feature.
   6 
   7 It assumes andesim and its engines are already installed and built
   8 (QEMU, the vsim engines, the plugin, the runtime, and the test ELFs are
   9 prebuilt). If something is missing, run `./andesim doctor` and hand the
  10 report to whoever owns your install; building is covered in `README.md`,
  11 not here.
  12 
  13 ---
  14 
  15 ## 1. What andesim is
  16 
  17 andesim runs one RISC-V ELF on one of three models:
  18 
  19 | Model    | What runs                              | Speed          | You get                    |
  20 |----------|----------------------------------------|----------------|-----------------------------|
  21 | `fast`   | QEMU only (functional)                 | MHz-class      | program output, fast        |
  22 | `cycle`  | one cycle-accurate engine, from reset  | kHz-class      | program output + total cycles |
  23 | `hybrid` | QEMU fast-forwards, then the cycle engine measures one region you choose | fast until your region | program output + cycles of JUST your region |
  24 
  25 `hybrid` is the headline feature: QEMU races through boot and setup, then
  26 hands the complete architectural state and memory to the cycle-accurate
  27 engine (vsim, built from the real RTL), which runs only your
  28 region-of-interest (ROI). The cycle figure is the vsim `mcycle` delta
  29 across that window. You mark the window with a **trigger**: source-level
  30 markers or a pair of PCs (section 5.3).
  31 
  32 One run models ONE core. The cycle engine defines the hardware (ISA,
  33 VLEN, caches); in hybrid mode the QEMU leg automatically inherits that
  34 engine's ISA and VLEN so both legs execute the same architecture.
  35 
  36 ---
  37 
  38 ## 2. Check your installation
  39 
  40 ```sh
  41 ./andesim doctor          # read-only health report
  42 ./andesim list models     # the three models
  43 ./andesim list engines    # every engine you can pass to --engine
  44 ```
  45 
  46 `doctor` checks artifacts, toolchain, runtime, engines, and the shared-memory
  47 backing tiers, and prints WSL2 advice where relevant. A healthy install ends
  48 with `Summary: N PASS, 0 FAIL`.
  49 
  50 `list engines` shows what `--engine` accepts:
  51 
  52 ```
  53 ENGINE                 TYPE  KIND            XLEN  VLEN  DLEN  ELEN
  54 qemu64                 qemu  functional      64    -     -     -
  55 qemu32                 qemu  functional      32    -     -     -
  56 vsim:ax45mpv_premium   vsim  cycle-accurate  64    512   512   32
  57 vsim:ax46mpv_advanced  vsim  cycle-accurate  64    512   512   32
  58 ```
  59 
  60 `qemu64`/`qemu32` are the functional engines (`fast`); the `vsim:<cfg>`
  61 entries are the cycle-accurate engines (`cycle`, and the measuring leg of
  62 `hybrid`). `-` means the engine does not report that parameter.
  63 
  64 Engines are discovered from the `sim_*` binaries in `VSIM_BIN_DIR` (set in
  65 `config.env` or the environment). Each binary supplies its capabilities and
  66 invocation templates through `--describe`, with `<binary>.json` as a fallback.
  67 No engine registration or per-build CSR manifest is required. Select an
  68 engine with `--engine` when multiple cycle-accurate engines are available;
  69 hybrid still requires a compatible RV64 engine and the shared state ABI.
  70 See [Engine interface](engine_interface.md) for the integration contract.
  71 
  72 Run `./andesim run -h` any time for the compact flag list; this guide is
  73 the long version.
  74 
  75 ---
  76 
  77 ## 3. First runs
  78 
  79 The install ships ready-made ELFs under `tests/fixtures/`; the examples
  80 below use them. Replace with your own ELF once you have one (section 4).
  81 
  82 ### 3.1 fast -- functional, full speed
  83 
  84 ```sh
  85 ./andesim run --mode fast tests/fixtures/vplat_hello.elf
  86 ```
  87 
  88 ```
  89 hello from vplat
  90 ```
  91 
  92 Output is the program's own output, verbatim (QEMU passthrough). The exit
  93 code of your program becomes the process exit code.
  94 
  95 ### 3.2 cycle -- one engine, from reset, total cycles
  96 
  97 ```sh
  98 ./andesim run --mode cycle --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium tests/fixtures/vplat_hello.elf
  99 ```
 100 
 101 ```
 102 hello from vplat
 103 [andesim] 4247 cycles
 104 ```
 105 
 106 The engine's startup banner and verbose info log are filtered out so the
 107 result stands alone; real warnings/errors still pass through, and the
 108 program's exit code is propagated. The figure is the whole run from reset
 109 -- boot, runtime init, everything.
 110 
 111 ### 3.3 hybrid -- fast-forward, then measure your region
 112 
 113 `hybrid` needs a trigger that says where the measured window starts and
 114 ends. The fixture below already contains ROI markers, so `--trigger
 115 marker` works out of the box:
 116 
 117 ```sh
 118 ./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium \
 119   tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf
 120 ```
 121 
 122 ```
 123 hello from QEMU1
 124 [andesim] 54 cycles
 125 ```
 126 
 127 Reading the output:
 128 
 129 - `hello from QEMU1` is the program's own output from the fast leg.
 130 - `[andesim] 54 cycles` is the answer: your ROI took 54 cycles on
 131   this engine. It is the vsim `mcycle` delta across the window (the same
 132   line shape `cycle` mode prints, but here it covers JUST your ROI).
 133 - The run ends after the ROI. Code after your ROI never executes in a
 134   hybrid run -- hybrid is a measuring tool, not a way to finish the program.
 135 - Want more detail? `--log-level 1` (section 5.10) adds the driver's
 136   chatter: the resolved engine/VLEN/trigger banner and the shared-memory
 137   line (`[andesim] mmap ...`, section 5.4).
 138 
 139 The first hybrid run of a given (engine, ELF) pair is a few seconds slower:
 140 andesim captures the engine's reset state once and caches it under
 141 `~/.cache/andesim/` so later runs can skip restoring registers that still
 142 hold reset values (typically ~4x faster on the vsim leg). The cache
 143 refreshes itself when the engine or the ELF changes.
 144 
 145 ---
 146 
 147 ## 4. Prepare your own program
 148 
 149 ### 4.1 Compile once, run on every engine
 150 
 151 Link against the andesim runtime and one ELF runs on `fast`, on `cycle`,
 152 and across a `hybrid` handoff -- no per-engine builds, no semihosting:
 153 
 154 ```sh
 155 riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O2 \
 156   -B <andesim>/build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs your_prog.c -o your_prog.elf
 157 ```
 158 
 159 - Use your Andes RISC-V GCC (the one `./andesim doctor` reports).
 160 - `-B` points gcc at the runtime artifacts; use the absolute path when
 161   compiling outside the repo.
 162 - `-specs=andesim.specs` swaps in the runtime's `crt0.o`, links
 163   `andesim.ld` (load base `0x00100000`), and pins the library order, so no
 164   semihosting library can leak into the link.
 165 - Add `v` to `-march` (e.g. `rv64gcv`) for RVV code.
 166 
 167 For rv32 targets use the rv32 compiler and the rv32 runtime flavor:
 168 
 169 ```sh
 170 riscv32-unknown-elf-gcc -march=rv32gc -mabi=ilp32d -O2 \
 171   -B <andesim>/build/runtime/rv32 -specs=andesim.specs your_prog.c -o your_prog.elf
 172 ```
 173 
 174 C++ works through the same two flags -- just switch the driver to `g++`:
 175 
 176 ```sh
 177 riscv64-unknown-elf-g++ -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O2 \
 178   -B <andesim>/build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs your_prog.cpp -o your_prog.elf
 179 ```
 180 
 181 - Static constructors run before `main` (crt0 walks `.init_array` via
 182   newlib's `__libc_init_array`), and returning from `main` has C++
 183   `exit(rc)` semantics: atexit handlers and static destructors run.
 184 - libstdc++ heap containers (`std::string`, `std::vector`, ...) sit on
 185   the runtime heap; the g++ driver adds `-lstdc++ -lm` itself, and the
 186   specs add `crtbegin/crtend`.
 187 - Prefer `printf` over `<iostream>`: iostreams add hundreds of KB of
 188   code and static-init work that noticeably lengthens a cycle-mode boot.
 189 
 190 Custom build system (no gcc driver)? Link the pieces directly:
 191 
 192 ```sh
 193 ... -nostartfiles -nodefaultlibs -T build/runtime/andesim.ld \
 194   build/runtime/crt0.o your_prog.o -L build/runtime \
 195   -Wl,--start-group -landesim_runtime -lc -lgcc -Wl,--end-group
 196 ```
 197 
 198 (For C++, add `crtbegin.o`/`crtend.o` around your objects and `-lstdc++
 199 -lm` before the group -- or just use the `g++` driver form above.)
 200 
 201 What the runtime gives your program, on every engine:
 202 
 203 | Channel          | Behavior                                                       |
 204 |------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------|
 205 | stdio (fd 0-2)   | `printf` etc. go to the simulator console (a modeled UART)     |
 206 | exit code        | `exit(n)` (n < 256) terminates the simulation; `n` becomes the simulator process exit code |
 207 | file io (fd > 2) | `open`/`read`/`write` pass through to host files, resolved against the engine's working directory |
 208 
 209 A `printf` inside a measured ROI works -- but it adds the real UART cycles
 210 to your figure. Keep measured kernels I/O-free when you want clean numbers.
 211 
 212 ### 4.2 Mark your region (ROI markers)
 213 
 214 For `--trigger marker`, wrap the region you want to measure:
 215 
 216 ```c
 217 #include <andesim/ROI.h>   /* shipped with the runtime; rides the -B flag */
 218 
 219 andesim_ROI_begin();
 220 my_kernel(a, b, c);
 221 andesim_ROI_end();
 222 ```
 223 
 224 The markers are RISC-V HINT instructions (architectural NOPs), so a marker
 225 binary also runs unchanged on `fast`, on `cycle`, and on real silicon.
 226 Ship one binary; measure when you want.
 227 
 228 > **Measurement hygiene:** keep the kernel anchored inside the marker span
 229 > -- read its inputs and write its outputs through memory inside the span,
 230 > or wrap the kernel in a `__attribute__((noinline))` function called
 231 > between the markers. The markers pin memory I/O but not register-only
 232 > compute, so a kernel that carries live values in registers across the
 233 > boundary may be hoisted or sunk out of the measured window by the
 234 > compiler.
 235 
 236 ### 4.3 Cannot edit the binary? Use PC boundaries
 237 
 238 `--trigger pc` needs no markers: you name the window with `--pc-start` and
 239 `--pc-end`, each a symbol name or a `0x` address (section 5.3). To find
 240 the hot region of an unknown binary first, run the profile command:
 241 
 242 ```sh
 243 ./andesim profile --min-iters 10 my_kernel.elf
 244 ```
 245 
 246 It runs the binary fast (QEMU, configured like your engine) and reports
 247 the hottest loops (function, source line, PCs) with a ready `measure:`
 248 line -- a `--pc-start`/`--pc-end` pair you can paste straight into the
 249 hybrid command. See section 6 and `docs/profile.md` for the full flag
 250 reference.
 251 
 252 ---
 253 
 254 ## 5. The `run` options, one by one
 255 
 256 Synopsis:
 257 
 258 ```
 259 ./andesim run --mode fast|cycle|hybrid [options] <ELF> [-- <engine args>]
 260 ```
 261 
 262 `run` is the default command -- you may omit it. `./andesim --mode fast
 263 my.elf` and `./andesim my.elf --mode fast` both work; only the explicit
 264 commands (`profile`, `list`, `doctor`) are recognized by name.
 265 
 266 ### 5.1 `--mode fast|cycle|hybrid` (required)
 267 
 268 Picks the model (section 1). Everything else keys off this choice.
 269 
 270 ### 5.2 `--engine <id>`
 271 
 272 Picks the engine from `./andesim list engines`.
 273 
 274 - `fast`: optional. The driver auto-selects `qemu64` or `qemu32` to match
 275   your ELF's width; an explicit `--engine qemu32|qemu64` overrides (with a
 276   warning if it disagrees with the ELF).
 277 - `cycle` / `hybrid`: names the cycle-accurate engine. Optional only when
 278   exactly one is installed; with several you must choose:
 279 
 280   ```
 281   andesim run --mode cycle: model cycle: multiple cycle-accurate engines;
 282   select one with --engine (have: vsim:ax45mpv_premium, vsim:ax46mpv_advanced)
 283   ```
 284 
 285 Width rules: `cycle`/`hybrid` reject an ELF whose width does not match the
 286 engine, up front:
 287 
 288 ```
 289 andesim run --mode cycle: ELF is rv32 but engine 'vsim:ax45mpv_premium' is rv64
 290   -- pick a matching engine or an rv64 ELF
 291 ```
 292 
 293 Hybrid additionally requires an rv64 engine (the fast leg is rv64; an rv32
 294 engine cannot share architectural state with it and is rejected).
 295 
 296 VLEN: each vsim engine has a fixed VLEN (see `list engines`); in hybrid
 297 mode the QEMU leg inherits the engine's ISA and VLEN automatically, so
 298 both legs execute identical architecture. Supported VLEN range in hybrid:
 299 128 to 1024 bits. A standalone `fast` run defaults to the vector-capable
 300 `andes-ax46mpv` (rv64) / `andes-a46mpv` (rv32) CPU model; to pin an exact
 301 VLEN there, append a `-cpu` through the passthrough tail (the last `-cpu`
 302 wins):
 303 
 304 ```sh
 305 ./andesim run --mode fast app.elf -- -cpu andes-ax46mpv,vlen=256
 306 ```
 307 
 308 ### 5.3 `--trigger marker|pc` (+ `--pc-start`, `--pc-end`) -- hybrid only, required
 309 
 310 The ROI delimiter for `--mode hybrid`.
 311 
 312 **`--trigger marker`** (recommended when you can edit the source): the
 313 window is the span strictly between `andesim_ROI_begin()` and
 314 `andesim_ROI_end()` (section 4.2). The markers themselves are NOPs and
 315 cost nothing.
 316 
 317 **`--trigger pc`**: explicit boundaries, no source edits. Both flags are
 318 required; each accepts a symbol name or a `0x` hex address:
 319 
 320 ```sh
 321 ./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger pc --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium \
 322   --pc-start vmatmul_kernel --pc-end 0x1002cc my.elf
 323 ```
 324 
 325 Semantics you should know:
 326 
 327 - The instruction at `--pc-start` executes INSIDE the measured window (the
 328   fast leg stops just before it; the cycle engine resumes at it -- no
 329   instruction is lost across the handoff). `--pc-end` is where the window
 330   closes.
 331 - Symbols are resolved from the ELF's own symbol table by the driver; no
 332   toolchain is needed at run time. A name that is not defined fails with
 333   `symbol '<x>' not defined in <elf>`; a bad literal fails with
 334   `malformed address '<x>'`.
 335 - Both triggers are one-shot: the first hit of the start boundary opens the
 336   window, the first hit of the end boundary closes it. For a function called
 337   many times, the window is the FIRST call.
 338 - Start and end must resolve to different addresses; an equal pair is an
 339   empty window and is rejected up front:
 340   `--pc-start and --pc-end resolve to the same address 0x... (an empty ROI measures nothing)`.
 341 
 342 ### 5.4 `--mem-size <spec>` -- guest memory
 343 
 344 `SPEC` accepts `256M`, `1.5G`, `2G`, or raw bytes. Per-model meaning:
 345 
 346 | Model    | Effect |
 347 |----------|--------|
 348 | `hybrid` | Your program RAM (default `128M`). Max `2G` minus 4 KiB: the driver reserves one page just above your RAM for the vector-register transport, so exactly `2G` is rejected (use `2047M`) and an ELF whose static image reaches into the reserved page is rejected with `raise --mem-size or shrink the image`. |
 349 | `fast`   | Forwarded as a plain QEMU `-m`. No 2G cap; QEMU validates the size itself. |
 350 | `cycle`  | Ignored (the engine always models its full DRAM window); the driver says so on stderr. |
 351 
 352 Where the hybrid shared memory lives: andesim allocates a file both legs
 353 map. It picks the first tier with enough free space (request + 256 MiB
 354 headroom); run with `--log-level 1` to see which:
 355 
 356 1. `/dev/shm` -- RAM-backed, fastest.
 357 2. `~/.cache/andesim` -- disk-backed fallback (honors `XDG_CACHE_HOME`).
 358 
 359 ```
 360 [andesim] mmap 2.0 GiB at /home/u/.cache/andesim (free: 2.1 TiB) (fallback: /dev/shm too small (1.2 GiB free))
 361 ```
 362 
 363 Set `HSIM_MMAP_DIR=/path` to pin one directory with NO fallback past it
 364 (the run fails with a hint if it cannot hold the request). Do not pin a
 365 tmpfs mount (`/tmp` on some distros) expecting a disk ceiling -- tmpfs is
 366 still RAM.
 367 
 368 ### 5.5 `--print-memmap` -- which addresses may a hybrid workload touch?
 369 
 370 Prints the guest memory map for exactly the run you are about to do (same
 371 `--engine`/`--mem-size`; the ELF is optional and only adds a fit note),
 372 then exits without running anything. Hybrid only.
 373 
 374 ```sh
 375 ./andesim run --mode hybrid --print-memmap --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium --mem-size 128M
 376 ```
 377 
 378 ```
 379 [andesim] hybrid memory map: engine=vsim:ax45mpv_premium mem-size=128M
 380 REGION           BASE         END          SIZE    TRANSPORT
 381 DRAM             0x0          0x7ffffff    128M    shared mmap; content survives the handoff
 382 V-scratch        0x8000000    0x8000fff    4K      reserved by the hybrid V transport; not program-usable
 383 ILM              0x0          0xffff       64K     sidecar .ilm; DRAM overlay while milmb.IEN=1
 384 DLM              0x200000     0x207fff     32K     sidecar .dlm; DRAM overlay while mdlmb.IEN=1
 385 HVM              0x90000000   0x9003ffff   256K    sidecar .hvm
 386 SimControl/HTIF  0xe0080000   0xe0080fff   4K      device; state does not cross the handoff
 387 UART2            0xf0300000   0xf03fffff   1M      device (console); state does not cross the handoff
 388 ```
 389 
 390 How to read it:
 391 
 392 - END is the inclusive last byte.
 393 - DRAM tracks `--mem-size`; the V-scratch page above it belongs to andesim.
 394 - ILM/DLM/HVM rows appear only when the chosen engine has those memories
 395   and can transport their content; the addresses are the engine's own.
 396 - Device state never crosses the handoff (each engine has its own UART and
 397   SimControl instance); only RAM content does.
 398 - Anything NOT listed is unsupported in hybrid mode: it exists in one
 399   engine only, so touching it inside the ROI gives engine-specific behavior.

1 # andesim User Guide
   2 
   3 Audience: an engineer who wants to RUN programs on the Andes simulators
   4 through `./andesim` and measure cycle counts. This guide covers every
   5 user-facing option and feature.
   6 
   7 It assumes andesim and its engines are already installed and built
   8 (QEMU, the vsim engines, the plugin, the runtime, and the test ELFs are
   9 prebuilt). If something is missing, run `./andesim doctor` and hand the
  10 report to whoever owns your install; building is covered in `README.md`,
  11 not here.
  12 
  13 ---
  14 
  15 ## 1. What andesim is
  16 
  17 andesim runs one RISC-V ELF on one of three models:
  18 
  19 | Model    | What runs                              | Speed          | You get                    |
  20 |----------|----------------------------------------|----------------|-----------------------------|
  21 | `fast`   | QEMU only (functional)                 | MHz-class      | program output, fast        |
  22 | `cycle`  | one cycle-accurate engine, from reset  | kHz-class      | program output + total cycles |
  23 | `hybrid` | QEMU fast-forwards, then the cycle engine measures one region you choose | fast until your region | program output + cycles of JUST your region |
  24 
  25 `hybrid` is the headline feature: QEMU races through boot and setup, then
  26 hands the complete architectural state and memory to the cycle-accurate
  27 engine (vsim, built from the real RTL), which runs only your
  28 region-of-interest (ROI). The cycle figure is the vsim `mcycle` delta
  29 across that window. You mark the window with a **trigger**: source-level
  30 markers or a pair of PCs (section 5.3).
  31 
  32 One run models ONE core. The cycle engine defines the hardware (ISA,
  33 VLEN, caches); in hybrid mode the QEMU leg automatically inherits that
  34 engine's ISA and VLEN so both legs execute the same architecture.
  35 
  36 ---
  37 
  38 ## 2. Check your installation
  39 
  40 ```sh
  41 ./andesim doctor          # read-only health report
  42 ./andesim list models     # the three models
  43 ./andesim list engines    # every engine you can pass to --engine
  44 ```
  45 
  46 `doctor` checks artifacts, toolchain, runtime, engines, and the shared-memory
  47 backing tiers, and prints WSL2 advice where relevant. A healthy install ends
  48 with `Summary: N PASS, 0 FAIL`.
  49 
  50 `list engines` shows what `--engine` accepts:
  51 
  52 ```
  53 ENGINE                 TYPE  KIND            XLEN  VLEN  DLEN  ELEN
  54 qemu64                 qemu  functional      64    -     -     -
  55 qemu32                 qemu  functional      32    -     -     -
  56 vsim:ax45mpv_premium   vsim  cycle-accurate  64    512   512   32
  57 vsim:ax46mpv_advanced  vsim  cycle-accurate  64    512   512   32
  58 ```
  59 
  60 `qemu64`/`qemu32` are the functional engines (`fast`); the `vsim:<cfg>`
  61 entries are the cycle-accurate engines (`cycle`, and the measuring leg of
  62 `hybrid`). `-` means the engine does not report that parameter.
  63 
  64 Engines are discovered from the `sim_*` binaries in `VSIM_BIN_DIR` (set in
  65 `config.env` or the environment). Each binary supplies its capabilities and
  66 invocation templates through `--describe`, with `<binary>.json` as a fallback.
  67 No engine registration or per-build CSR manifest is required. Select an
  68 engine with `--engine` when multiple cycle-accurate engines are available;
  69 hybrid still requires a compatible RV64 engine and the shared state ABI.
  70 See [Engine interface](engine_interface.md) for the integration contract.
  71 
  72 Run `./andesim run -h` any time for the compact flag list; this guide is
  73 the long version.
  74 
  75 ---
  76 
  77 ## 3. First runs
  78 
  79 The install ships ready-made ELFs under `tests/fixtures/`; the examples
  80 below use them. Replace with your own ELF once you have one (section 4).
  81 
  82 ### 3.1 fast -- functional, full speed
  83 
  84 ```sh
  85 ./andesim run --mode fast tests/fixtures/vplat_hello.elf
  86 ```
  87 
  88 ```
  89 hello from vplat
  90 ```
  91 
  92 Output is the program's own output, verbatim (QEMU passthrough). The exit
  93 code of your program becomes the process exit code.
  94 
  95 ### 3.2 cycle -- one engine, from reset, total cycles
  96 
  97 ```sh
  98 ./andesim run --mode cycle --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium tests/fixtures/vplat_hello.elf
  99 ```
 100 
 101 ```
 102 hello from vplat
 103 [andesim] 4247 cycles
 104 ```
 105 
 106 The engine's startup banner and verbose info log are filtered out so the
 107 result stands alone; real warnings/errors still pass through, and the
 108 program's exit code is propagated. The figure is the whole run from reset
 109 -- boot, runtime init, everything.
 110 
 111 ### 3.3 hybrid -- fast-forward, then measure your region
 112 
 113 `hybrid` needs a trigger that says where the measured window starts and
 114 ends. The fixture below already contains ROI markers, so `--trigger
 115 marker` works out of the box:
 116 
 117 ```sh
 118 ./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium \
 119   tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf
 120 ```
 121 
 122 ```
 123 hello from QEMU1
 124 [andesim] 54 cycles
 125 ```

 130 - `[andesim] 54 cycles` is the answer: your ROI took 54 cycles on
 131   this engine. It is the vsim `mcycle` delta across the window (the same
 132   line shape `cycle` mode prints, but here it covers JUST your ROI).
 133 - The run ends after the ROI. Code after your ROI never executes in a
 134   hybrid run -- hybrid is a measuring tool, not a way to finish the program.

 321 ./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger pc --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium \
 322   --pc-start vmatmul_kernel --pc-end 0x1002cc my.elf
 323 ```
 324 
 325 Semantics you should know:
 326 
 327 - The instruction at `--pc-start` executes INSIDE the measured window (the
 328   fast leg stops just before it; the cycle engine resumes at it -- no
 329   instruction is lost across the handoff). `--pc-end` is where the window
 330   closes.
 331 - Symbols are resolved from the ELF's own symbol table by the driver; no
 332   toolchain is needed at run time. A name that is not defined fails with
 333   `symbol '<x>' not defined in <elf>`; a bad literal fails with
 334   `malformed address '<x>'`.
 335 - Both triggers are one-shot: the first hit of the start boundary opens the
 336   window, the first hit of the end boundary closes it. For a function called
 337   many times, the window is the FIRST call.
 338 - Start and end must resolve to different addresses; an equal pair is an
 339   empty window and is rejected up front:
 340   `--pc-start and --pc-end resolve to the same address 0x... (an empty ROI measures nothing)`.
 341 
 342 ### 5.4 `--mem-size <spec>` -- guest memory
 343 
 344 `SPEC` accepts `256M`, `1.5G`, `2G`, or raw bytes. Per-model meaning:
 345 
 346 | Model    | Effect |
 347 |----------|--------|
 348 | `hybrid` | Your program RAM (default `128M`). Max `2G` minus 4 KiB: the driver reserves one page just above your RAM for the vector-register transport, so exactly `2G` is rejected (use `2047M`) and an ELF whose static image reaches into the reserved page is rejected with `raise --mem-size or shrink the image`. |
 349 | `fast`   | Forwarded as a plain QEMU `-m`. No 2G cap; QEMU validates the size itself. |
 350 | `cycle`  | Ignored (the engine always models its full DRAM window); the driver says so on stderr. |
 351 
 352 Where the hybrid shared memory lives: andesim allocates a file both legs
 353 map. It picks the first tier with enough free space (request + 256 MiB
 354 headroom); run with `--log-level 1` to see which:
 355 
 356 1. `/dev/shm` -- RAM-backed, fastest.
 357 2. `~/.cache/andesim` -- disk-backed fallback (honors `XDG_CACHE_HOME`).
 358 
 359 ```
 360 [andesim] mmap 2.0 GiB at /home/u/.cache/andesim (free: 2.1 TiB) (fallback: /dev/shm too small (1.2 GiB free))
 361 ```
 362 
 363 Set `HSIM_MMAP_DIR=/path` to pin one directory with NO fallback past it
 364 (the run fails with a hint if it cannot hold the request). Do not pin a
 365 tmpfs mount (`/tmp` on some distros) expecting a disk ceiling -- tmpfs is
 366 still RAM.
 367 
 368 ### 5.5 `--print-memmap` -- which addresses may a hybrid workload touch?
 369 
 370 Prints the guest memory map for exactly the run you are about to do (same
 371 `--engine`/`--mem-size`; the ELF is optional and only adds a fit note),
 372 then exits without running anything. Hybrid only.
 373 
 374 ```sh
 375 ./andesim run --mode hybrid --print-memmap --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium --mem-size 128M
 376 ```
 377 
 378 ```
 379 [andesim] hybrid memory map: engine=vsim:ax45mpv_premium mem-size=128M
 380 REGION           BASE         END          SIZE    TRANSPORT
 381 DRAM             0x0          0x7ffffff    128M    shared mmap; content survives the handoff
 382 V-scratch        0x8000000    0x8000fff    4K      reserved by the hybrid V transport; not program-usable
 383 ILM              0x0          0xffff       64K     sidecar .ilm; DRAM overlay while milmb.IEN=1
 384 DLM              0x200000     0x207fff     32K     sidecar .dlm; DRAM overlay while mdlmb.IEN=1
 385 HVM              0x90000000   0x9003ffff   256K    sidecar .hvm
 386 SimControl/HTIF  0xe0080000   0xe0080fff   4K      device; state does not cross the handoff
 387 UART2            0xf0300000   0xf03fffff   1M      device (console); state does not cross the handoff
 388 ```
 389 
 390 How to read it:
 391 
 392 - END is the inclusive last byte.
 393 - DRAM tracks `--mem-size`; the V-scratch page above it belongs to andesim.
 394 - ILM/DLM/HVM rows appear only when the chosen engine has those memories
 395   and can transport their content; the addresses are the engine's own.
 396 - Device state never crosses the handoff (each engine has its own UART and
 397   SimControl instance); only RAM content does.
 398 - Anything NOT listed is unsupported in hybrid mode: it exists in one
 399   engine only, so touching it inside the ROI gives engine-specific behavior.

 413 # # command 2/2: accurate-leg [vsim:ax45mpv_premium]

 415 ```

 417 ### 5.7 `--verify` -- cross-check a hybrid run against a QEMU oracle
 418 
 419 A hybrid run normally proves only that a cycle figure came out. `--verify`
 420 (hybrid only, default off) re-runs the same ELF on pure QEMU up to the ROI
 421 exit and compares the architectural state field by field against what the
 422 cycle engine drained:
 423 
 424 ```
 425 [andesim] 46 cycles
 426 [state-diff] PASS: 109 fields match (counters and passthrough CSRs excluded)
 427 [verify] PASS: vsim drain matches the QEMU oracle
 428 ```
 429 
 430 A mismatch lists each differing field and exits non-zero:
 431 
 432 ```
 433 [state-diff] x10: ref=0x3d got=0x0
 434 [state-diff] FAIL: 1 mismatch(es) (115 fields compared)
 435 ```
 436 
 437 What is compared: the PC, all GPRs, FPRs (when FP state is live), the
 438 vector registers and V CSRs (when V is live), the privilege level, and the
 439 M-mode CSRs that round-trip through the handoff. On an S-mode-capable
 440 engine (one whose `--describe` names them, e.g. `vsim:ax66_makatau`) the
 441 S/U trap CSRs `satp`, `medeleg`, and `mideleg` also round-trip and are
 442 compared. Deliberately excluded: `mcycle`/`minstret` (the engines count
 443 differently by design), `mip` (hardware-driven pending bits), and a few
 444 CSRs whose reset values legitimately differ between engines.
 445 
 446 Two costs: one extra QEMU run of the whole program (cheap), and a full
 447 register read-back over the Debug Module at the ROI exit (not cheap --
 448 without `--verify` the exit drain reads only the two counters). Expect a
 449 `--verify` run to take noticeably longer; the cycle figure itself is not
 450 affected.
 451 
 452 Related, printed on EVERY hybrid run (not just `--verify`): andesim tracks
 453 which config CSRs your program actually wrote during the fast leg and
 454 warns if any of them do not exist on the chosen cycle engine:
 455 
 456 ```
 457 [andesim] warning: the program wrote CSRs engine vsim:<engine> does not
 458 implement: <names> (on this engine's silicon these writes would trap; the
 459 hybrid restore skipped them)
 460 ```
 461 
 462 That means your program, on that engine's real silicon, would trap before
 463 the ROI -- pick an engine that implements those CSRs, or drop the writes.
 464 A clean run prints nothing.
 465 
 466 ### 5.8 `--kanata <file>` (+ `--objdump <file>`) -- pipeline trace of the ROI
 467 
 468 Hybrid only (`--trigger marker|pc`). Writes a Kanata-format pipeline trace
 469 covering exactly the measured window -- engine boot and handoff overhead
 470 are filtered out. Open the file in
 471 [Konata](https://github.com/shioyadan/Konata) to see the pipeline.
 472 
 473 ```sh
 474 ./andesim run tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul.elf \
 475   --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium \
 476   --kanata /tmp/roi.kanata
 477 ```
 478 
 479 Add `--objdump <file>` (a text dump you generated once with
 480 `riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump -d my.elf > my.S`) and the trace embeds the
 481 disassembly next to each PC. `--objdump` requires `--kanata`.
 482 
 483 Marker-mode constraint: the ELF must contain exactly one exit marker. With
 484 more than one, the run errors out and tells you to use `--trigger pc` with
 485 an explicit `--pc-end` instead.
 486 
 487 ### 5.9 `--gdb` (+ `--gdb-port <port>`) -- attach a debugger
 488 
 489 Pauses the simulation at startup so a debugger can attach. Not available
 490 in hybrid mode.
 491 
 492 **fast** -- opens QEMU's GDB stub (default port 1234) and waits:
 493 
 494 ```sh
 495 ./andesim run --mode fast --gdb my.elf
 496 # other terminal:
 497 gdb-multiarch -ex 'target remote :1234' my.elf
 498 ```
 499 
 500 **cycle** -- resets and HALTS the hart, opens the engine's JTAG bitbang
 501 port (default 9104) in the background, then execs `$ICEMAN` -- your JTAG
 502 debug server -- in the foreground. Point GDB at the server's own gdb port
 503 (from your server config), not at 9104:
 504 
 505 ```sh
 506 export ICEMAN=/path/to/jtag-debug-server
 507 ./andesim run --mode cycle --gdb --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium my.elf
 508 ```
 509 
 510 `$ICEMAN` must speak the OpenOCD `remote_bitbang` protocol. A modern
 511 **OpenOCD (0.12+)** works: a one-line wrapper can `exec openocd -f <cfg>`
 512 where `<cfg>` sets `adapter driver remote_bitbang`, `remote_bitbang port
 513 9104`, a generic `riscv` target, and a `gdb_port`. Note: the OpenOCD 0.10
 514 bundled with Andes ICEman has a `remote_bitbang` bug against this DTM --
 515 use a current OpenOCD.
 516 
 517 `--gdb-port` overrides the port (fast: the QEMU stub port; cycle: the
 518 JTAG bitbang port).
 519 
 520 ### 5.10 `--log-level <0-6>` (+ `--log-file`) -- how much andesim says
 521 
 522 The same scale as the vsim engines' own `--log-level`, so you learn one
 523 scheme: `0=trace 1=debug 2=info 3=warn 4=error 5=critical 6=off`.
 524 Default is `2` (info): you see your program's output, the answer line
 525 (`[andesim] N cycles`), and any warnings or errors -- nothing else.
 526 
 527 `--log-level 1` (debug) adds the driver's chatter: the hybrid banner
 528 (engine/VLEN/trigger), the decision lines (which engine and why; what
 529 your `--pc-start`/`--pc-end` resolved to), the shared-mmap line (section
 530 5.4), the window detail (`[andesim] window: trigger=... vsim mcycle=...
 531 qemu mcycle=...`), and the closing PASS line. The level also rides into
 532 both hybrid legs: the vsim engine gets the same `--log-level`, the QEMU
 533 handoff plugin gets `log_level=`, and their stderr streams live to your
 534 terminal (at info and above it is silenced), so one flag tunes the whole
 535 pipeline.
 536 
 537 `--log-level 0` (trace) additionally prints, just before each engine
 538 spawns, its fully resolved command line -- the hybrid legs (`[andesim]
 539 exec fast-leg [qemu64]: ...`) and the standalone fast/cycle runs
 540 (`[andesim] exec standalone [qemu64]: ...`) alike. It is the same text
 541 `--dry-run` shows, copy-pasteable to re-run one engine by hand, and it
 542 is emitted BEFORE the spawn, so even a hung run leaves the command in
 543 the log.
 544 
 545 `--log-file <file>` appends EVERY level's messages -- timestamped and
 546 level-tagged, regardless of the console `--log-level` -- to `<file>`.
 547 Run once with `--log-file`, attach the file to a bug report, and nothing
 548 needs re-running. Your program's own output is never filtered at any
 549 level.
 550 
 551 Related (always on, any level): when a hybrid leg fails, andesim keeps
 552 the run's evidence -- the drained state files, LM sidecars, the staged
 553 QEMU config, a copy of your ELF, and a `manifest.txt` with the error and
 554 every leg's exact command -- under `~/.cache/andesim/repro/` (newest 20
 555 kept) and prints where:
 556 
 557 ```
 558 [andesim] repro: kept run artifacts at /home/u/.cache/andesim/repro/20260711T081500Z-my_prog (see manifest.txt)
 559 ```
 560 
 561 ### 5.11 `--step-timeout-ms <ms>` -- hybrid only, raise the per-leg timeout
 562 
 563 Each hybrid leg (the fast QEMU handoff, the cycle-accurate vsim ROI) is
 564 spawned with a timeout; the default is `90000` (90s), enough for every
 565 fixture-scale ROI. A real, unabridged compute kernel -- a full-size
 566 transformer matmul, for instance -- can legitimately need minutes on the
 567 ~9 kHz cycle-accurate leg. If a hybrid run fails with `plan step N: timed
 568 out after <ms> ms`, that is not necessarily a hang: raise the budget and
 569 re-run before assuming a bug.
 570 
 571 ```sh
 572 ./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --step-timeout-ms 900000 my.elf
 573 ```
 574 
 575 The value must be a positive integer (milliseconds); anything else is a
 576 clean `--step-timeout-ms: not a positive integer: <value>` error.
 577 
 578 ### 5.12 `-- <args...>` -- engine passthrough
 579 
 580 Everything after a bare `--` is forwarded verbatim to the engine.
 581 `fast`/`cycle` only: those modes run one engine process, so there is an
 582 unambiguous target (see the VLEN example in 5.2). `hybrid` builds both
 583 legs' command lines itself and REJECTS `--` args rather than guessing
 584 which leg you meant -- use the dedicated flags (`--kanata`, `--objdump`,
 585 `--mem-size`, ...) instead.
 586 
 587 ### 5.13 `--runtime linux` -- run a static-glibc binary under the vlinux proxy kernel
 588 
 589 Status: `--mode fast` and `--mode hybrid` (`cycle` is rejected -- no roadmap
 590 need for it; see `ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md`).
 591 
 592 ```sh
 593 ./andesim run --mode fast --runtime linux app.elf
 594 ```
 595 
 596 The ELF you pass is your **app**, not a bare-metal image: andesim stages a
 597 private copy of the `vlinux.elf` proxy kernel (built by `scripts/build_all.sh
 598 vlinux`), stamps your app's absolute path and `--mem-size` into its
 599 `.manifest` section via `objcopy --update-section`, and boots THAT staged
 600 copy instead of your app directly. This needs `HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN` set (env or
 601 `config.env`) to run `objcopy`.
 602 
 603 Two defaults change under `--runtime linux`:
 604 - `--mem-size` defaults to `1G` (instead of QEMU's own default) -- override it
 605   the normal way if your app needs more or less.
 606 - The CPU is pinned to the engine-synced `andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512` (instead of
 607   the standalone-fast default `andes-ax46mpv`), so a fast run matches the
 608   hardware a later hybrid measurement would target.
 609 
 610 vlinux loads your app's PT_LOAD segments, builds the Linux initial stack
 611 (argc/argv/envp/auxv) and jumps to its entry point in M-mode, so it runs like
 612 an ordinary freestanding Linux-ABI ELF. `argv[0]` is your app's own path;
 613 `-- <args...>` becomes argv[1..] (e.g. `-- -m model.gguf -t 1`), up to 64
 614 extra args / 4096 total bytes. envp is always empty -- no test needs it yet.
 615 
 616 A real static-glibc binary now runs: it reaches `main()`, `malloc`/`mmap`/
 617 `brk` work, `printf`-style I/O goes out through vlinux's UART, and ordinary
 618 host-file I/O works -- `fopen`/`fread`/`fwrite`/`fseek`/`ftell`, `open`/
 619 `openat`/`close`/`read`/`pread64`/`lseek`, `fstat`/`fstatat`/`statx` (basic
 620 fields: mode, size, nlink, uid/gid), `faccessat`, `getcwd`. Files are opened
 621 relative to the engine process's own working directory, same as the vplat
 622 runtime's file I/O. Not implemented: symlinks (`readlinkat` always returns
 623 `EINVAL`) and directory listing (`getdents64` always returns `ENOSYS`).
 624 `clock_gettime(CLOCK_REALTIME/CLOCK_MONOTONIC)`, `clock_getres`,
 625 `nanosleep`/`clock_nanosleep` also work -- the pattern `ggml_time_us()`
 626 (llama.cpp's own timing helper) uses -- so timing code compiles and runs
 627 unpatched; `nanosleep` returns immediately (there is no timer, so a sleep
 628 burns no simulated time) and the values are HOST wall time, meaningful on
 629 the fast leg but not inside a vsim ROI (the cycle count is the answer
 630 there). File-backed `mmap(fd, MAP_PRIVATE or MAP_SHARED, PROT_READ, ...)`
 631 -- llama.cpp's own GGUF load path uses `MAP_SHARED` -- also works: the
 632 file's range is eagerly read into a private, independently-owned copy at
 633 mmap time (there is no on-demand paging here, no MMU). A `MAP_SHARED`
 634 mapping is only accepted without `PROT_WRITE`: for a read-only mapping
 635 there is no observable difference from `MAP_PRIVATE` (the distinction is
 636 entirely about write visibility), but a writable `MAP_SHARED` request has
 637 no host-file write-back path and is refused (`ENOSYS`). `munmap`
 638 (including a partial/tail unmap of an already-mapped range) always
 639 succeeds without actually reclaiming space, matching POSIX's own
 640 "unmapping unmapped memory is not an error" rule. `mremap` always fails
 641 (`ENOMEM`) rather than attempt an in-place grow this allocator cannot do.
 642 `sysinfo`, `fadvise64`/`madvise` (access-pattern hints -- there is no
 643 readahead/cache policy to tune, so both are accepted no-ops) and `futex`
 644 also work: `futex` always answers "available"/"0 waiters", which is safe
 645 and spec-legal precisely because there is only one hart -- real
 646 concurrency never exists to make that wrong. This does NOT mean threads
 647 work: `clone`/`clone3` are `ENOSYS` (no threads,
 648 `ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md`'s own non-goal), so `pthread_create` still
 649 fails -- code that does not gracefully handle that failure will crash.
 650 Known gap:
 651 glibc's `exit()` (the library call -- not the raw exit syscall) crashes while
 652 running its own internal cleanup-handler list, on what looks like a vendor
 653 riscv64 toolchain issue (see `ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md` U4 for the full
 654 investigation); a program that calls the raw `_exit()`/`_Exit()` instead
 655 exits cleanly today. Any other unimplemented syscall prints
 656 `vlinux: ENOSYS <nr>` once and returns -ENOSYS rather than crashing.
 657 
 658 **Under `--mode hybrid`**: `--trigger marker` works --
 659 `<andesim/ROI.h>`'s `andesim_ROI_begin()`/`andesim_ROI_end()` around any
 660 region of your app measures it cycle-accurately, exactly like a bare-metal
 661 marker'd fixture. One thing happens automatically that is worth knowing:
 662 vsim's own trigger only scans the ELF it is told to BOOT (here, the staged
 663 vlinux-run.elf) for the marker instructions -- but the markers are in
 664 YOUR app, which vlinux only loads into memory at runtime, never part of
 665 vlinux-run.elf's own static content. andesim resolves your app's real
 666 exit-marker address itself and passes it to vsim directly, so this is
 667 transparent -- you do not need `--trigger pc` or to know the address
 668 yourself. `--mem-size` defaults to `1G` here too. See section 11 for a
 669 full walkthrough building up to a real llama.cpp kernel measurement.
 670 Track progress in `ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md`.
 671 
 672 ---
 673 
 674 ## 6. The `profile` command -- find your ROI first
 675 
 676 When you do not yet know WHERE the hot region is, run `profile` before
 677 `run --mode hybrid`:
 678 
 679 ```sh
 680 ./andesim profile [--engine <id>] my_kernel.elf
 681 ```
 682 
 683 It runs the whole ELF under QEMU with a loop-detector plugin
 684 (`libhotIterationLoop.so`) and prints a Markdown report of the hottest
 685 loops. Each loop block ends with a ready window:
 686 
 687 ```
 688 measure:      --pc-start 0x10007c --pc-end 0x1000c2  (all of vadd_kernel: entry -> ret)
 689 ```
 690 
 691 Paste that pair into `./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger pc ...` to
 692 measure exactly that function on the cycle engine.
 693 
 694 profile picks its engine the same way hybrid does (`--engine <id>`, or
 695 the sole installed cycle-accurate engine) and launches QEMU with THAT
 696 engine's configuration -- the same `-cpu`/`-readconfig` sync a hybrid
 697 fast leg gets. So the loop ranking reflects the ISA (including VLEN) of
 698 the engine you will measure on.
 699 
 700 Useful knobs: `--min-iters <N>` drops cold loops, `--limit <N>` caps the
 701 report, `--no-optimize-rvv` also shows scalar loops (the default reports
 702 RVV-containing loops only), `--no-llm` prints a plain table, `--dry-run`
 703 previews the QEMU command. Full reference: `docs/profile.md`.
 704 
 705 ---
 706 
 707 ## 7. What a hybrid run does for you automatically
 708 
 709 You normally do not need this section to use andesim -- it explains the
 710 behaviors you will observe.
 711 
 712 **Two legs, one state.** The fast leg (QEMU) runs to your ROI start, then
 713 drains the complete architectural state -- GPRs, FPRs, vector registers,
 714 CSRs (including the Andes-specific blocks), privilege level -- into a
 715 state file. Program RAM is shared by construction (both legs map the same
 716 file), so memory needs no copy. The cycle engine restores the state
 717 through its Debug Module, runs your ROI, and drains the counters at the
 718 exit trigger. The cycle figure is the vsim `mcycle` delta.
 719 
 720 **Config that matters for timing rides along.** Cache-enable state (L1
 721 `mcache_ctl`, and the L2 controller's config window on engines that have
 722 an L2) is restored before the ROI, so a program that enabled caches during
 723 boot measures WITH caches on -- not at the engine's reset default.
 724 
 725 **Only what your program wrote is restored.** andesim records which config
 726 CSRs the program actually wrote during the fast leg and restores only
 727 those; an untouched CSR keeps the engine's own reset value, exactly like
 728 that engine's real silicon. If the program wrote a CSR the engine does not
 729 implement, you get the warning shown in section 5.7.
 730 
 731 **Local memories travel too.** On engines with ILM/DLM (tightly-coupled
 732 memories) or HVM (high-bandwidth vector memory), their content is drained
 733 from the fast leg and loaded into the cycle engine before resume, so a
 734 program that stages code or data there before the ROI resumes with it in
 735 place. (A program using ILM/DLM must enable them itself via
 736 `milmb`/`mdlmb`, as real TCM firmware does; that write is restored
 737 automatically.) `--print-memmap` shows whether your engine has these
 738 regions.
 739 
 740 **First-run baseline capture.** Restoring a register over the Debug Module
 741 costs hundreds of simulated cycles, and most state still holds reset
 742 values. The first hybrid run of a given (engine build, ELF) pair captures
 743 the engine's reset state once and caches it under `~/.cache/andesim/`
 744 (honors `XDG_CACHE_HOME`); later runs skip the no-op restores, typically
 745 cutting the vsim leg ~4x. The cache invalidates itself when the engine or
 746 ELF changes; delete the directory to force a fresh capture. This never
 747 changes results -- a restore is skipped only when the value is already
 748 there.
 749

 452 Related, printed on EVERY hybrid run (not just `--verify`): andesim tracks
 453 which config CSRs your program actually wrote during the fast leg and
 454 warns if any of them do not exist on the chosen cycle engine:
 455 
 456 ```
 457 [andesim] warning: the program wrote CSRs engine vsim:<engine> does not
 458 implement: <names> (on this engine's silicon these writes would trap; the
 459 hybrid restore skipped them)
 460 ```
 461 
 462 That means your program, on that engine's real silicon, would trap before
 463 the ROI -- pick an engine that implements those CSRs, or drop the writes.
 464 A clean run prints nothing.
 465 
 466 ### 5.8 `--kanata <file>` (+ `--objdump <file>`) -- pipeline trace of the ROI
 467 
 468 Hybrid only (`--trigger marker|pc`). Writes a Kanata-format pipeline trace
 469 covering exactly the measured window -- engine boot and handoff overhead
 470 are filtered out. Open the file in
 471 [Konata](https://github.com/shioyadan/Konata) to see the pipeline.
 472 
 473 ```sh
 474 ./andesim run tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul.elf \
 475   --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium \
 476   --kanata /tmp/roi.kanata
 477 ```
 478 
 479 Add `--objdump <file>` (a text dump you generated once with
 480 `riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump -d my.elf > my.S`) and the trace embeds the
 481 disassembly next to each PC. `--objdump` requires `--kanata`.
 482 
 483 Marker-mode constraint: the ELF must contain exactly one exit marker. With
 484 more than one, the run errors out and tells you to use `--trigger pc` with
 485 an explicit `--pc-end` instead.
 486 
 487 ### 5.9 `--gdb` (+ `--gdb-port <port>`) -- attach a debugger
 488 
 489 Pauses the simulation at startup so a debugger can attach. Not available
 490 in hybrid mode.
 491 
 492 **fast** -- opens QEMU's GDB stub (default port 1234) and waits:
 493 
 494 ```sh
 495 ./andesim run --mode fast --gdb my.elf
 496 # other terminal:
 497 gdb-multiarch -ex 'target remote :1234' my.elf
 498 ```
 499 
 500 **cycle** -- resets and HALTS the hart, opens the engine's JTAG bitbang
 501 port (default 9104) in the background, then execs `$ICEMAN` -- your JTAG
 502 debug server -- in the foreground. Point GDB at the server's own gdb port
 503 (from your server config), not at 9104:
 504 
 505 ```sh
 506 export ICEMAN=/path/to/jtag-debug-server
 507 ./andesim run --mode cycle --gdb --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium my.elf
 508 ```
 509 
 510 `$ICEMAN` must speak the OpenOCD `remote_bitbang` protocol. A modern
 511 **OpenOCD (0.12+)** works: a one-line wrapper can `exec openocd -f <cfg>`
 512 where `<cfg>` sets `adapter driver remote_bitbang`, `remote_bitbang port
 513 9104`, a generic `riscv` target, and a `gdb_port`. Note: the OpenOCD 0.10
 514 bundled with Andes ICEman has a `remote_bitbang` bug against this DTM --
 515 use a current OpenOCD.
 516 
 517 `--gdb-port` overrides the port (fast: the QEMU stub port; cycle: the
 518 JTAG bitbang port).
 519 
 520 ### 5.10 `--log-level <0-6>` (+ `--log-file`) -- how much andesim says
 521 
 522 The same scale as the vsim engines' own `--log-level`, so you learn one
 523 scheme: `0=trace 1=debug 2=info 3=warn 4=error 5=critical 6=off`.
 524 Default is `2` (info): you see your program's output, the answer line
 525 (`[andesim] N cycles`), and any warnings or errors -- nothing else.
 526 
 527 `--log-level 1` (debug) adds the driver's chatter: the hybrid banner
 528 (engine/VLEN/trigger), the decision lines (which engine and why; what
 529 your `--pc-start`/`--pc-end` resolved to), the shared-mmap line (section
 530 5.4), the window detail (`[andesim] window: trigger=... vsim mcycle=...
 531 qemu mcycle=...`), and the closing PASS line. The level also rides into
 532 both hybrid legs: the vsim engine gets the same `--log-level`, the QEMU
 533 handoff plugin gets `log_level=`, and their stderr streams live to your
 534 terminal (at info and above it is silenced), so one flag tunes the whole
 535 pipeline.
 536 
 537 `--log-level 0` (trace) additionally prints, just before each engine
 538 spawns, its fully resolved command line -- the hybrid legs (`[andesim]
 539 exec fast-leg [qemu64]: ...`) and the standalone fast/cycle runs
 540 (`[andesim] exec standalone [qemu64]: ...`) alike. It is the same text
 541 `--dry-run` shows, copy-pasteable to re-run one engine by hand, and it
 542 is emitted BEFORE the spawn, so even a hung run leaves the command in
 543 the log.
 544 
 545 `--log-file <file>` appends EVERY level's messages -- timestamped and
 546 level-tagged, regardless of the console `--log-level` -- to `<file>`.
 547 Run once with `--log-file`, attach the file to a bug report, and nothing
 548 needs re-running. Your program's own output is never filtered at any
 549 level.
 550 
 551 Related (always on, any level): when a hybrid leg fails, andesim keeps
 552 the run's evidence -- the drained state files, LM sidecars, the staged
 553 QEMU config, a copy of your ELF, and a `manifest.txt` with the error and
 554 every leg's exact command -- under `~/.cache/andesim/repro/` (newest 20
 555 kept) and prints where:
 556 
 557 ```
 558 [andesim] repro: kept run artifacts at /home/u/.cache/andesim/repro/20260711T081500Z-my_prog (see manifest.txt)
 559 ```
 560 
 561 ### 5.11 `--step-timeout-ms <ms>` -- hybrid only, raise the per-leg timeout
 562 
 563 Each hybrid leg (the fast QEMU handoff, the cycle-accurate vsim ROI) is
 564 spawned with a timeout; the default is `90000` (90s), enough for every
 565 fixture-scale ROI. A real, unabridged compute kernel -- a full-size
 566 transformer matmul, for instance -- can legitimately need minutes on the
 567 ~9 kHz cycle-accurate leg. If a hybrid run fails with `plan step N: timed
 568 out after <ms> ms`, that is not necessarily a hang: raise the budget and
 569 re-run before assuming a bug.
 570 
 571 ```sh
 572 ./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --step-timeout-ms 900000 my.elf
 573 ```
 574 
 575 The value must be a positive integer (milliseconds); anything else is a
 576 clean `--step-timeout-ms: not a positive integer: <value>` error.
 577 
 578 ### 5.12 `-- <args...>` -- engine passthrough
 579 
 580 Everything after a bare `--` is forwarded verbatim to the engine.
 581 `fast`/`cycle` only: those modes run one engine process, so there is an
 582 unambiguous target (see the VLEN example in 5.2). `hybrid` builds both
 583 legs' command lines itself and REJECTS `--` args rather than guessing
 584 which leg you meant -- use the dedicated flags (`--kanata`, `--objdump`,
 585 `--mem-size`, ...) instead.
 586 
 587 ### 5.13 `--runtime linux` -- run a static-glibc binary under the vlinux proxy kernel
 588 
 589 Status: `--mode fast` and `--mode hybrid` (`cycle` is rejected -- no roadmap
 590 need for it; see `ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md`).
 591 
 592 ```sh
 593 ./andesim run --mode fast --runtime linux app.elf
 594 ```
 595 
 596 The ELF you pass is your **app**, not a bare-metal image: andesim stages a
 597 private copy of the `vlinux.elf` proxy kernel (built by `scripts/build_all.sh
 598 vlinux`), stamps your app's absolute path and `--mem-size` into its
 599 `.manifest` section via `objcopy --update-section`, and boots THAT staged
 600 copy instead of your app directly. This needs `HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN` set (env or
 601 `config.env`) to run `objcopy`.
 602 
 603 Two defaults change under `--runtime linux`:
 604 - `--mem-size` defaults to `1G` (instead of QEMU's own default) -- override it
 605   the normal way if your app needs more or less.
 606 - The CPU is pinned to the engine-synced `andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512` (instead of
 607   the standalone-fast default `andes-ax46mpv`), so a fast run matches the
 608   hardware a later hybrid measurement would target.
 609 
 610 vlinux loads your app's PT_LOAD segments, builds the Linux initial stack
 611 (argc/argv/envp/auxv) and jumps to its entry point in M-mode, so it runs like
 612 an ordinary freestanding Linux-ABI ELF. `argv[0]` is your app's own path;
 613 `-- <args...>` becomes argv[1..] (e.g. `-- -m model.gguf -t 1`), up to 64
 614 extra args / 4096 total bytes. envp is always empty -- no test needs it yet.
 615 
 616 A real static-glibc binary now runs: it reaches `main()`, `malloc`/`mmap`/
 617 `brk` work, `printf`-style I/O goes out through vlinux's UART, and ordinary
 618 host-file I/O works -- `fopen`/`fread`/`fwrite`/`fseek`/`ftell`, `open`/
 619 `openat`/`close`/`read`/`pread64`/`lseek`, `fstat`/`fstatat`/`statx` (basic
 620 fields: mode, size, nlink, uid/gid), `faccessat`, `getcwd`. Files are opened
 621 relative to the engine process's own working directory, same as the vplat
 622 runtime's file I/O. Not implemented: symlinks (`readlinkat` always returns
 623 `EINVAL`) and directory listing (`getdents64` always returns `ENOSYS`).
 624 `clock_gettime(CLOCK_REALTIME/CLOCK_MONOTONIC)`, `clock_getres`,
 625 `nanosleep`/`clock_nanosleep` also work -- the pattern `ggml_time_us()`
 626 (llama.cpp's own timing helper) uses -- so timing code compiles and runs
 627 unpatched; `nanosleep` returns immediately (there is no timer, so a sleep
 628 burns no simulated time) and the values are HOST wall time, meaningful on
 629 the fast leg but not inside a vsim ROI (the cycle count is the answer
 630 there). File-backed `mmap(fd, MAP_PRIVATE or MAP_SHARED, PROT_READ, ...)`
 631 -- llama.cpp's own GGUF load path uses `MAP_SHARED` -- also works: the
 632 file's range is eagerly read into a private, independently-owned copy at
 633 mmap time (there is no on-demand paging here, no MMU). A `MAP_SHARED`
 634 mapping is only accepted without `PROT_WRITE`: for a read-only mapping
 635 there is no observable difference from `MAP_PRIVATE` (the distinction is
 636 entirely about write visibility), but a writable `MAP_SHARED` request has
 637 no host-file write-back path and is refused (`ENOSYS`). `munmap`
 638 (including a partial/tail unmap of an already-mapped range) always
 639 succeeds without actually reclaiming space, matching POSIX's own
 640 "unmapping unmapped memory is not an error" rule. `mremap` always fails
 641 (`ENOMEM`) rather than attempt an in-place grow this allocator cannot do.
 642 `sysinfo`, `fadvise64`/`madvise` (access-pattern hints -- there is no
 643 readahead/cache policy to tune, so both are accepted no-ops) and `futex`
 644 also work: `futex` always answers "available"/"0 waiters", which is safe
 645 and spec-legal precisely because there is only one hart -- real
 646 concurrency never exists to make that wrong. This does NOT mean threads
 647 work: `clone`/`clone3` are `ENOSYS` (no threads,
 648 `ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md`'s own non-goal), so `pthread_create` still
 649 fails -- code that does not gracefully handle that failure will crash.
 650 Known gap:
 651 glibc's `exit()` (the library call -- not the raw exit syscall) crashes while
 652 running its own internal cleanup-handler list, on what looks like a vendor
 653 riscv64 toolchain issue (see `ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md` U4 for the full
 654 investigation); a program that calls the raw `_exit()`/`_Exit()` instead
 655 exits cleanly today. Any other unimplemented syscall prints
 656 `vlinux: ENOSYS <nr>` once and returns -ENOSYS rather than crashing.
 657 
 658 **Under `--mode hybrid`**: `--trigger marker` works --
 659 `<andesim/ROI.h>`'s `andesim_ROI_begin()`/`andesim_ROI_end()` around any
 660 region of your app measures it cycle-accurately, exactly like a bare-metal
 661 marker'd fixture. One thing happens automatically that is worth knowing:
 662 vsim's own trigger only scans the ELF it is told to BOOT (here, the staged
 663 vlinux-run.elf) for the marker instructions -- but the markers are in
 664 YOUR app, which vlinux only loads into memory at runtime, never part of
 665 vlinux-run.elf's own static content. andesim resolves your app's real
 666 exit-marker address itself and passes it to vsim directly, so this is
 667 transparent -- you do not need `--trigger pc` or to know the address
 668 yourself. `--mem-size` defaults to `1G` here too. See section 11 for a
 669 full walkthrough building up to a real llama.cpp kernel measurement.
 670 Track progress in `ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md`.
 671 
 672 ---
 673 
 674 ## 6. The `profile` command -- find your ROI first
 675 
 676 When you do not yet know WHERE the hot region is, run `profile` before
 677 `run --mode hybrid`:
 678 
 679 ```sh
 680 ./andesim profile [--engine <id>] my_kernel.elf
 681 ```
 682 
 683 It runs the whole ELF under QEMU with a loop-detector plugin
 684 (`libhotIterationLoop.so`) and prints a Markdown report of the hottest
 685 loops. Each loop block ends with a ready window:
 686 
 687 ```
 688 measure:      --pc-start 0x10007c --pc-end 0x1000c2  (all of vadd_kernel: entry -> ret)
 689 ```
 690 
 691 Paste that pair into `./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger pc ...` to
 692 measure exactly that function on the cycle engine.
 693 
 694 profile picks its engine the same way hybrid does (`--engine <id>`, or
 695 the sole installed cycle-accurate engine) and launches QEMU with THAT
 696 engine's configuration -- the same `-cpu`/`-readconfig` sync a hybrid
 697 fast leg gets. So the loop ranking reflects the ISA (including VLEN) of
 698 the engine you will measure on.
 699 
 700 Useful knobs: `--min-iters <N>` drops cold loops, `--limit <N>` caps the
 701 report, `--no-optimize-rvv` also shows scalar loops (the default reports
 702 RVV-containing loops only), `--no-llm` prints a plain table, `--dry-run`
 703 previews the QEMU command. Full reference: `docs/profile.md`.
 704 
 705 ---
 706 
 707 ## 7. What a hybrid run does for you automatically
 708 
 709 You normally do not need this section to use andesim -- it explains the
 710 behaviors you will observe.
 711 
 712 **Two legs, one state.** The fast leg (QEMU) runs to your ROI start, then
 713 drains the complete architectural state -- GPRs, FPRs, vector registers,
 714 CSRs (including the Andes-specific blocks), privilege level -- into a
 715 state file. Program RAM is shared by construction (both legs map the same
 716 file), so memory needs no copy. The cycle engine restores the state
 717 through its Debug Module, runs your ROI, and drains the counters at the
 718 exit trigger. The cycle figure is the vsim `mcycle` delta.
 719 
 720 **Config that matters for timing rides along.** Cache-enable state (L1
 721 `mcache_ctl`, and the L2 controller's config window on engines that have
 722 an L2) is restored before the ROI, so a program that enabled caches during
 723 boot measures WITH caches on -- not at the engine's reset default.
 724 
 725 **Only what your program wrote is restored.** andesim records which config
 726 CSRs the program actually wrote during the fast leg and restores only
 727 those; an untouched CSR keeps the engine's own reset value, exactly like
 728 that engine's real silicon. If the program wrote a CSR the engine does not
 729 implement, you get the warning shown in section 5.7.
 730 
 731 **Local memories travel too.** On engines with ILM/DLM (tightly-coupled
 732 memories) or HVM (high-bandwidth vector memory), their content is drained
 733 from the fast leg and loaded into the cycle engine before resume, so a
 734 program that stages code or data there before the ROI resumes with it in
 735 place. (A program using ILM/DLM must enable them itself via
 736 `milmb`/`mdlmb`, as real TCM firmware does; that write is restored
 737 automatically.) `--print-memmap` shows whether your engine has these
 738 regions.
 739 
 740 **First-run baseline capture.** Restoring a register over the Debug Module
 741 costs hundreds of simulated cycles, and most state still holds reset
 742 values. The first hybrid run of a given (engine build, ELF) pair captures
 743 the engine's reset state once and caches it under `~/.cache/andesim/`
 744 (honors `XDG_CACHE_HOME`); later runs skip the no-op restores, typically
 745 cutting the vsim leg ~4x. The cache invalidates itself when the engine or
 746 ELF changes; delete the directory to force a fresh capture. This never
 747 changes results -- a restore is skipped only when the value is already
 748 there.
 749
