750 **The ROI envelope (limits).** The measured window is assumed bare-metal,
 751 single-hart, trap-free, interrupt-free, paging-off, and single-privilege.
 752 The S/U trap CSRs `satp`, `medeleg`, and `mideleg` are transported on
 753 S-mode-capable engines (so an in-ROI read sees your values); other S-mode
 754 CSRs (`sstatus`, `sepc`, ...) are not transported yet. The privilege level
 755 itself IS carried: an S/U-mode handoff also mirrors the PMP configuration
 756 and requires an S/U-capable engine -- on an M-mode-only engine the resume
 757 aborts with a clear pick-another-engine error. A workload that traps,
 758 takes an interrupt, or switches privilege inside the ROI is outside the
 759 contract. And because there is no hand-back leg, nothing after the ROI
 760 executes.
 761 
 762 ---
 763 
 764 ## 8. Running on WSL2 and macOS
 765 
 766 **Linux** -- native, nothing to do.
 767 
 768 **Windows (WSL2)** -- works as Linux; two caveats:
 769 
 770 - Keep the repo and the mmap directories on the ext4 side (`~/...`), never
 771   under `/mnt/c` (drvfs is slow and shared mappings are not coherent there).
 772 - `/dev/shm` is capped by the WSL VM memory. Raise `memory=` in
 773   `%UserProfile%\.wslconfig` if tier 1 is too small -- or let the tier list
 774   fall through to `~/.cache/andesim` automatically.
 775 
 776 `./andesim doctor` checks both (see its `mmap tiers:` section and WSL
 777 warnings).
 778 
 779 **macOS** -- run-only. The engines are Linux binaries, so `./andesim`
 780 transparently re-execs the run inside a prebuilt Linux runtime image in
 781 the podman machine VM. One-time setup:
 782 
 783 ```sh
 784 brew install podman
 785 podman machine init --memory 4096
 786 podman machine start
 787 podman pull <runtime image>      # or load a CI-built andesim-runtime:latest
 788 ./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --mem-size 256M my.elf
 789 ```
 790 
 791 Knobs: `ANDESIM_IMAGE` (image name, default `andesim-runtime:latest`),
 792 `ANDESIM_SHM_SIZE` (container `/dev/shm`, default `3g`),
 793 `ANDESIM_CONTAINER_ENGINE` (podman/docker). Your current directory is
 794 bind-mounted at the same path, so relative ELF paths and output files
 795 work. Apple Silicon runs the x86-64 image under emulation -- expect slower
 796 wall-clock than a Linux host.
 797 
 798 ---
 799 
 800 ## 9. Troubleshooting
 801 
 802 | Symptom | Meaning / fix |
 803 |---------|----------------|
 804 | `multiple cycle-accurate engines; select one with --engine (have: ...)` | More than one engine is installed. Add `--engine <id>` from `list engines`. |
 805 | `ELF is rv32 but engine '...' is rv64 -- pick a matching engine or an rv64 ELF` | Width mismatch caught up front. Rebuild the ELF for the engine's width or pick the other engine. |
 806 | `--trigger marker\|pc is required (the ROI delimiter; ...)` | Hybrid always needs the ROI delimiter: `--trigger marker` (markers in source) or `--trigger pc --pc-start S --pc-end E`. |
 807 | The run never reaches the ROI / hangs until timeout | The start trigger never fired: the binary has no markers (marker mode), or `--pc-start` is never executed. Check with `--trigger pc` on a PC you know retires, or run `./andesim profile` to find real hot PCs. |
 808 | `symbol '<x>' not defined in <elf>` / `malformed address '<x>'` | `--pc-start`/`--pc-end` must be a defined symbol or a valid `0x` literal. |
 809 | `--pc-start and --pc-end resolve to the same address ... (an empty ROI measures nothing)` | Pick two distinct boundaries; equal ones would measure nothing. |
 810 | `--mem-size ...` rejected, or `raise --mem-size or shrink the image` | Hybrid caps at `2G` minus 4 KiB (use `2047M`), and the ELF's static image must fit below the reserved V-scratch page. |
 811 | The mmap chose a disk directory (`[andesim] mmap ...` at `--log-level 1`), or `HSIM_MMAP_DIR` run fails | `/dev/shm` was too small for the request. Either accept the disk tier, free RAM, or pin a big non-tmpfs directory via `HSIM_MMAP_DIR`. |
 812 | `warning: the program wrote CSRs engine ... does not implement: ...` | The figure may not represent this program on this engine (on silicon those writes would trap). Choose an engine implementing those CSRs, or drop the writes. |
 813 | `multiple ... markers in ELF -- use --mode hybrid --trigger pc ...` (with `--kanata`) | Kanata needs a unique exit; switch to `--trigger pc` and name the exit with `--pc-end`. |
 814 | `hybrid` rejects `-- <args>` | By design: hybrid owns both legs' command lines. Use the dedicated flags instead. |
 815 | Missing artifact / engine not discovered | Run `./andesim doctor`; it names exactly what is missing and where it looked. Setup/build is covered in `README.md`. |
 816 | A hybrid leg failed and you want to report or debug it | The run printed `[andesim] repro: kept run artifacts at <dir>` -- that directory holds the evidence and `manifest.txt` has each leg's exact command (newest 20 kept). Re-run with `--log-file run.log` (and `--log-level 1` for live engine logs) for the full picture. |
 817 
 818 ---

 833 ## 11. Walkthrough: llama.cpp text generation under vlinux
 834 
 835 `ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md` U8: a real static-glibc `llama-completion`
 836 (llama.cpp's text-generation CLI) generating real text under `--runtime
 837 linux` on the fast leg -- verified working end to end (`-n 32`) against
 838 Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf, prompted with "The capital of France is":
 839 
 840 > The capital of France is Paris. Paris is the second-largest city in
 841 > France, with a population of over 1.8 million. Paris is located in the
 842 > Île-de-France
 843 
 844 (Bonsai-4B-Q1_0 is an extreme 1-bit quantization -- "second-largest" is a
 845 model-quality artifact, not an andesim/vlinux correctness issue; the
 846 point here is that a real 4B-parameter model's real GGUF loading,
 847 tokenization, RVV matrix math, and sampling all produced coherent,
 848 on-topic English text end to end.) This needs the vendor static-glibc
 849 `LINUX_TOOLCHAIN` (`config.env`/env; see section 5.13) and a checkout of
 850 [llama.cpp](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp).
 851 
 852 ### Build
 853 
 854 A fresh **static** build, separate from any dynamic build you may already
 855 have (a dynamic build cannot run here -- there is no dynamic linker under
 856 vlinux):
 857 
 858 ```sh
 859 TC=$LINUX_TOOLCHAIN   # the static-glibc toolchain, config.env's LINUX_TOOLCHAIN
 860 cmake -B build-rv64-static \
 861   -DCMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME=Linux -DCMAKE_SYSTEM_PROCESSOR=riscv64 \
 862   -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=$TC/bin/riscv64-linux-gcc \
 863   -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=$TC/bin/riscv64-linux-g++ \
 864   -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
 865   -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS=-mext-zvlsseg -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS=-mext-zvlsseg \
 866   -DCMAKE_EXE_LINKER_FLAGS=-static \
 867   -DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS=OFF \
 868   -DGGML_RV_ZFH=OFF -DGGML_RV_ZVFH=OFF -DGGML_CPU_REPACK=OFF \
 869   -DGGML_OPENMP=OFF -DGGML_NATIVE=OFF \
 870   -DLLAMA_CURL=OFF -DLLAMA_BUILD_COMMON=ON -DLLAMA_BUILD_TOOLS=ON
 871 
 872 cmake --build build-rv64-static -j$(nproc) --target llama-completion
 873 ```
 874 
 875 What each non-obvious flag is for:
 876 - `-static` (the linker flag, not just `BUILD_SHARED_LIBS=OFF`): without
 877   it the binary still dynamically links libc/libstdc++/the dynamic
 878   linker itself -- there is no dynamic linker under vlinux, so this is
 879   required, not optional.
 880 - `-mext-zvlsseg`: the Andes toolchain gates RVV segment-load/store
 881   intrinsics behind this flag; ggml's RVV kernels use them.
 882 - `GGML_RV_ZFH=OFF GGML_RV_ZVFH=OFF`: the target engine (`ax45mpv_premium`,
 883   ELEN=32) has no scalar or vector half-precision float support; leaving
 884   these on produces code that traps.
 885 - `GGML_CPU_REPACK=OFF`: repacking picks tensor layouts tuned for
 886   specific microarchitectures vlinux is not modeling.
 887 - `GGML_OPENMP=OFF`: no OpenMP runtime here. This does NOT remove
 888   threading -- ggml's CPU backend still spawns its own thread pool via
 889   `pthread_create` when `-t` asks for more than one thread. vlinux has no
 890   `clone`/`clone3` support (no threads, ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md's own
 891   non-goal), so **always pass `-t 1`** at run time.
 892 - `LLAMA_CURL=OFF`: no network stack here; only needed for llama.cpp's
 893   optional model-download-by-URL feature.
 894 
 895 **One required source patch**, independent of `-t 1`: llama.cpp's own
 896 async status logger (`common/log.cpp`) spawns a background `std::thread`
 897 unconditionally, on the FIRST log call, regardless of `-t` -- and the
 898 generated completion text itself is printed through this same logger
 899 (`LOG("%s", token_str.c_str())`), not a separate direct-stdout path, so
 900 it cannot simply be avoided or ignored. Since `clone` is `ENOSYS` here,
 901 that `std::thread` construction throws `std::system_error`, uncaught,
 902 crashing the process before `main()`'s own code ever runs. This is a
 903 genuine upstream robustness gap (a background-logging performance
 904 optimization should not be able to crash the whole program if thread
 905 creation fails, on ANY platform), not a vlinux-specific issue -- fixed by
 906 catching the construction failure in `common_log::resume()` and falling
 907 back to printing synchronously from `add()` instead of queueing for a
 908 worker that will never run. Apply this patch to your llama.cpp checkout
 909 before building:
 910 
 911 ```diff
 912 --- a/common/log.cpp
 913 +++ b/common/log.cpp
 914 @@ struct common_log {
 915      bool prefix;
 916      bool timestamps;
 917      bool running;
 918 +    bool synchronous = false; // true if the worker thread could not be
 919 +                              // created (e.g. no thread support on this
 920 +                              // platform) -- add() prints inline instead
 921 @@ void add(...) {
 922          ...
 923          entry.timestamp = 0;
 924          if (timestamps) {
 925              entry.timestamp = t_us() - t_start;
 926          }
 927 
 928 +        if (synchronous) {
 929 +            // No worker thread exists (see resume()) -- print immediately
 930 +            // rather than queueing for a consumer that will never run.
 931 +            print_entry(entry);
 932 +            return;
 933 +        }
 934 +
 935          tail = (tail + 1) % queue.size();
 936          cv_new.notify_one();
 937      }
 938 
 939      void resume() {
 940          ...
 941          running = true;
 942 
 943 -        thrd = std::thread([this]() {
 944 -            ...
 945 -        });
 946 +        try {
 947 +            thrd = std::thread([this]() {
 948 +                ...
 949 +            });
 950 +        } catch (const std::system_error &) {
 951 +            synchronous = true;
 952 +        }
 953      }
 954 
 955      void pause() {
 956          {
 957              ...
 958              running = false;
 959 
 960 +            if (synchronous) {
 961 +                return; // no worker thread exists to signal/join
 962 +            }
 963 +
 964              // push an entry to signal the worker thread to stop
 965              ...
 966 ```
 967 
 968 (the `...` markers stand for unchanged surrounding code; see
 969 `common/log.cpp`'s `add()`/`resume()`/`pause()` methods for exact
 970 context.)
 971 
 972 ### Run
 973 
 974 ```sh
 975 ./andesim run --mode fast --runtime linux --mem-size 2G \
 976   build-rv64-static/bin/llama-completion \
 977   -- -m models/Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf -no-cnv \
 978      --prompt "The capital of France is" -n 32 -c 512 -t 1
 979 ```
 980 
 981 **`--mem-size 2G`, not the `1G` `--runtime linux` default** (section
 982 5.13): the model's own file-backed mmap (572 MB) plus its KV cache buffer
 983 (576 MB at `-c 512`) together exceed 1G -- found by direct measurement,
 984 not assumed; the roadmap's original "1G covers it" estimate did not
 985 account for the KV cache. `-c 512` (context size) keeps that KV cache
 986 buffer small and predictable; the default (`-c 0`, "loaded from model")
 987 would size it off Bonsai-4B's trained context (32768), needing much more
 988 memory for no benefit on a short prompt.
 989 
 990 Text streams out through vlinux's UART as it generates. Measured on one
 991 host: model load ~93s, prompt eval + a handful of tokens several more
 992 minutes -- QEMU's functional (not accelerated) emulation of real RVV
 993 matrix math on a real 4B-parameter model is slow by design (fast mode
 994 trades speed for cycle-independent correctness, not throughput); `-n 32`
 995 scales roughly linearly with token count. `exit()`'s known cleanup-handler
 996 crash (section 5.13) means the process may show that exact crash
 997 signature instead of a clean exit code -- the generated text itself is
 998 unaffected either way (it is printed well before `exit()` runs).
 999 
1000 `tests/vlinux/test_vlinux_llama_smoke.sh` automates this whole recipe
1001 (manual-tier -- not part of `scripts/run_e2e.sh`; needs `LINUX_TOOLCHAIN`,
1002 a pre-built `llama-completion`, and the GGUF model, all `config.env`-driven
1003 via `LLAMA_CPP_DIR`/`LLAMA_COMPLETION_BIN`/`BONSAI_GGUF`).
1004 
1005 ### Measuring one kernel iteration under hybrid mode
1006 
1007 The fast leg above proves correctness; `--mode hybrid` measures real
1008 cycles for one kernel iteration -- a full token would take hours at
1009 vsim's cycle-accurate clock (~9 kHz) even for a model this size, which is
1010 why hybrid mode exists: everything up to the marker runs on the fast
1011 QEMU leg (negligible time), and only the marked region runs on the
1012 cycle-accurate leg.
1013 
1014 ```sh
1015 ./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --runtime linux --mem-size 2000M \
1016   --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium --step-timeout-ms 900000 \
1017   build-rv64-static/bin/llama-completion \
1018   -- -m models/Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf -no-cnv \
1019      --prompt "The capital of France is" -n 32 -c 512 -t 1
1020 ```
1021 
1022 (`--mem-size` stays under 2G -- the AE350 DRAM window's actual usable
1023 ceiling is 2 GiB minus the V-scratch reservation, so `2000M` not `2G`.
1024 `--step-timeout-ms` raises the per-leg spawn timeout past its 90s
1025 default -- a real matmul on the cycle-accurate leg needs minutes; see the
1026 `--step-timeout-ms` line in section 5.)
1027 
1028 This needs `<andesim/ROI.h>` markers inside llama.cpp, bounding ONE
1029 matvec-class operation (not a whole token) -- see `docs/llama_roi_howto.md`
1030 for the exact patch and how the insertion point was chosen. Since ggml
1031 builds its whole computation graph before executing it in one shot,
1032 individual operations are not distinguishable at the application call-site
1033 level (e.g. the per-layer forward-pass code) -- the markers go in ggml's
1034 own generic per-node dispatch loop instead, gated by a counter so only
1035 one specific node's execution is actually measured.
1036 
1037 Confirmed end to end (2026-07-16): the command above, targeting layer 7's
1038 V-projection matmul (the smallest matmul shape in this architecture --
1039 see `docs/llama_roi_howto.md` for how the target node was chosen and why
1040 the first, larger pick timed out even at 15 minutes), measured
1041 **6528953 cycles**, identical across two independent runs (this hart is
1042 deterministic single-hart, so a stable repeat cycle count is the
1043 correctness signal, the same contract the small matvec fixture above it
1044 already demonstrates). QEMU's hybrid leg enforces the real engine's
1045 ELEN=32 vector-unit limit (unlike fast mode's own unconstrained CPU
1046 string) -- getting a real llama.cpp build through it needed four small,
1047 targeted upstream fixes to `ggml/src/ggml-cpu/{vec.cpp,arch/riscv/quants.c}`,
1048 documented in `docs/llama_roi_howto.md` together with the exact
1049 `ANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K` value and the reasoning for picking it.
1050 
1051 Also confirmed on `vsim:ax46mpv_fpga_l3` (ELEN=64, VLEN=1024): the same
1052 K=51 node, **4476168 cycles**, with the PRISTINE upstream `ggml` source --
1053 none of the ELEN=32 fixes above are needed on this engine, since its real
1054 vector unit natively supports what those fixes route around. This engine
1055 needs a different, unrelated build-flag fix (its real ISA lacks Zcd,
1056 compressed double-FP load/store) and a much larger `--step-timeout-ms`
1057 (its cycle-accurate leg is far slower in wall-clock terms). See
1058 `docs/llama_roi_howto.md` section 8 for the exact recipe.

 822 - `docs/hybrid_marker_quickstart.ipynb` -- runnable notebook version of
 823   the hybrid + marker flow, with captured real output (serve it with
 824   `scripts/notebook_server.sh`).
 825 - `docs/switching_modes_tutorial.md` -- one guided exercise per trigger
 826   mode, with drill-down on the underlying commands.
 827 - `docs/profile.md` -- the `profile` command's full reference (the
 828   hotIterationLoop detector).
 829 - `docs/engine_interface.md` -- how a new simulator joins andesim (for
 830   engine vendors/integrators, not needed to run workloads).
 831 - `README.md` -- what the workspace contains and how it is built.
 832 
 833 ## 11. Walkthrough: llama.cpp text generation under vlinux
 834 
 835 `ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md` U8: a real static-glibc `llama-completion`
 836 (llama.cpp's text-generation CLI) generating real text under `--runtime
 837 linux` on the fast leg -- verified working end to end (`-n 32`) against
 838 Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf, prompted with "The capital of France is":
 839 
 840 > The capital of France is Paris. Paris is the second-largest city in
 841 > France, with a population of over 1.8 million. Paris is located in the
 842 > Île-de-France
 843 
 844 (Bonsai-4B-Q1_0 is an extreme 1-bit quantization -- "second-largest" is a
 845 model-quality artifact, not an andesim/vlinux correctness issue; the
 846 point here is that a real 4B-parameter model's real GGUF loading,
 847 tokenization, RVV matrix math, and sampling all produced coherent,
 848 on-topic English text end to end.) This needs the vendor static-glibc
 849 `LINUX_TOOLCHAIN` (`config.env`/env; see section 5.13) and a checkout of
 850 [llama.cpp](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp).
 851 
 852 ### Build
 853 
 854 A fresh **static** build, separate from any dynamic build you may already
 855 have (a dynamic build cannot run here -- there is no dynamic linker under
 856 vlinux):
 857 
 858 ```sh
 859 TC=$LINUX_TOOLCHAIN   # the static-glibc toolchain, config.env's LINUX_TOOLCHAIN
 860 cmake -B build-rv64-static \
 861   -DCMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME=Linux -DCMAKE_SYSTEM_PROCESSOR=riscv64 \
 862   -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=$TC/bin/riscv64-linux-gcc \
 863   -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=$TC/bin/riscv64-linux-g++ \
 864   -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
 865   -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS=-mext-zvlsseg -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS=-mext-zvlsseg \
 866   -DCMAKE_EXE_LINKER_FLAGS=-static \
 867   -DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS=OFF \
 868   -DGGML_RV_ZFH=OFF -DGGML_RV_ZVFH=OFF -DGGML_CPU_REPACK=OFF \
 869   -DGGML_OPENMP=OFF -DGGML_NATIVE=OFF \
 870   -DLLAMA_CURL=OFF -DLLAMA_BUILD_COMMON=ON -DLLAMA_BUILD_TOOLS=ON
 871 
 872 cmake --build build-rv64-static -j$(nproc) --target llama-completion
 873 ```
 874 
 875 What each non-obvious flag is for:
 876 - `-static` (the linker flag, not just `BUILD_SHARED_LIBS=OFF`): without
 877   it the binary still dynamically links libc/libstdc++/the dynamic
 878   linker itself -- there is no dynamic linker under vlinux, so this is
 879   required, not optional.
 880 - `-mext-zvlsseg`: the Andes toolchain gates RVV segment-load/store
 881   intrinsics behind this flag; ggml's RVV kernels use them.
 882 - `GGML_RV_ZFH=OFF GGML_RV_ZVFH=OFF`: the target engine (`ax45mpv_premium`,
 883   ELEN=32) has no scalar or vector half-precision float support; leaving
 884   these on produces code that traps.
 885 - `GGML_CPU_REPACK=OFF`: repacking picks tensor layouts tuned for
 886   specific microarchitectures vlinux is not modeling.
 887 - `GGML_OPENMP=OFF`: no OpenMP runtime here. This does NOT remove
 888   threading -- ggml's CPU backend still spawns its own thread pool via
 889   `pthread_create` when `-t` asks for more than one thread. vlinux has no
 890   `clone`/`clone3` support (no threads, ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md's own
 891   non-goal), so **always pass `-t 1`** at run time.
 892 - `LLAMA_CURL=OFF`: no network stack here; only needed for llama.cpp's
 893   optional model-download-by-URL feature.
 894 
 895 **One required source patch**, independent of `-t 1`: llama.cpp's own
 896 async status logger (`common/log.cpp`) spawns a background `std::thread`
 897 unconditionally, on the FIRST log call, regardless of `-t` -- and the
 898 generated completion text itself is printed through this same logger
 899 (`LOG("%s", token_str.c_str())`), not a separate direct-stdout path, so
 900 it cannot simply be avoided or ignored. Since `clone` is `ENOSYS` here,
 901 that `std::thread` construction throws `std::system_error`, uncaught,
 902 crashing the process before `main()`'s own code ever runs. This is a
 903 genuine upstream robustness gap (a background-logging performance
 904 optimization should not be able to crash the whole program if thread
 905 creation fails, on ANY platform), not a vlinux-specific issue -- fixed by
 906 catching the construction failure in `common_log::resume()` and falling
 907 back to printing synchronously from `add()` instead of queueing for a
 908 worker that will never run. Apply this patch to your llama.cpp checkout
 909 before building:
 910 
 911 ```diff
 912 --- a/common/log.cpp
 913 +++ b/common/log.cpp
 914 @@ struct common_log {
 915      bool prefix;
 916      bool timestamps;
 917      bool running;
 918 +    bool synchronous = false; // true if the worker thread could not be
 919 +                              // created (e.g. no thread support on this
 920 +                              // platform) -- add() prints inline instead
 921 @@ void add(...) {
 922          ...
 923          entry.timestamp = 0;
 924          if (timestamps) {
 925              entry.timestamp = t_us() - t_start;
 926          }
 927 
 928 +        if (synchronous) {
 929 +            // No worker thread exists (see resume()) -- print immediately
 930 +            // rather than queueing for a consumer that will never run.
 931 +            print_entry(entry);
 932 +            return;
 933 +        }
 934 +
 935          tail = (tail + 1) % queue.size();
 936          cv_new.notify_one();
 937      }
 938 
 939      void resume() {
 940          ...
 941          running = true;
 942 
 943 -        thrd = std::thread([this]() {
 944 -            ...
 945 -        });
 946 +        try {
 947 +            thrd = std::thread([this]() {
 948 +                ...
 949 +            });
 950 +        } catch (const std::system_error &) {
 951 +            synchronous = true;
 952 +        }
 953      }
 954 
 955      void pause() {
 956          {
 957              ...
 958              running = false;
 959 
 960 +            if (synchronous) {
 961 +                return; // no worker thread exists to signal/join
 962 +            }
 963 +
 964              // push an entry to signal the worker thread to stop
 965              ...
 966 ```
 967 
 968 (the `...` markers stand for unchanged surrounding code; see
 969 `common/log.cpp`'s `add()`/`resume()`/`pause()` methods for exact
 970 context.)
 971 
 972 ### Run
 973 
 974 ```sh
 975 ./andesim run --mode fast --runtime linux --mem-size 2G \
 976   build-rv64-static/bin/llama-completion \
 977   -- -m models/Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf -no-cnv \
 978      --prompt "The capital of France is" -n 32 -c 512 -t 1
 979 ```
 980 
 981 **`--mem-size 2G`, not the `1G` `--runtime linux` default** (section
 982 5.13): the model's own file-backed mmap (572 MB) plus its KV cache buffer
 983 (576 MB at `-c 512`) together exceed 1G -- found by direct measurement,
 984 not assumed; the roadmap's original "1G covers it" estimate did not
 985 account for the KV cache. `-c 512` (context size) keeps that KV cache
 986 buffer small and predictable; the default (`-c 0`, "loaded from model")
 987 would size it off Bonsai-4B's trained context (32768), needing much more
 988 memory for no benefit on a short prompt.
 989 
 990 Text streams out through vlinux's UART as it generates. Measured on one
 991 host: model load ~93s, prompt eval + a handful of tokens several more
 992 minutes -- QEMU's functional (not accelerated) emulation of real RVV
 993 matrix math on a real 4B-parameter model is slow by design (fast mode
 994 trades speed for cycle-independent correctness, not throughput); `-n 32`
 995 scales roughly linearly with token count. `exit()`'s known cleanup-handler
 996 crash (section 5.13) means the process may show that exact crash
 997 signature instead of a clean exit code -- the generated text itself is
 998 unaffected either way (it is printed well before `exit()` runs).
 999 
1000 `tests/vlinux/test_vlinux_llama_smoke.sh` automates this whole recipe
1001 (manual-tier -- not part of `scripts/run_e2e.sh`; needs `LINUX_TOOLCHAIN`,
1002 a pre-built `llama-completion`, and the GGUF model, all `config.env`-driven
1003 via `LLAMA_CPP_DIR`/`LLAMA_COMPLETION_BIN`/`BONSAI_GGUF`).
1004 
1005 ### Measuring one kernel iteration under hybrid mode
1006 
1007 The fast leg above proves correctness; `--mode hybrid` measures real
1008 cycles for one kernel iteration -- a full token would take hours at
1009 vsim's cycle-accurate clock (~9 kHz) even for a model this size, which is
1010 why hybrid mode exists: everything up to the marker runs on the fast
1011 QEMU leg (negligible time), and only the marked region runs on the
1012 cycle-accurate leg.
1013 
1014 ```sh
1015 ./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --runtime linux --mem-size 2000M \
1016   --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium --step-timeout-ms 900000 \
1017   build-rv64-static/bin/llama-completion \
1018   -- -m models/Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf -no-cnv \
1019      --prompt "The capital of France is" -n 32 -c 512 -t 1
1020 ```
1021 
1022 (`--mem-size` stays under 2G -- the AE350 DRAM window's actual usable
1023 ceiling is 2 GiB minus the V-scratch reservation, so `2000M` not `2G`.
1024 `--step-timeout-ms` raises the per-leg spawn timeout past its 90s
1025 default -- a real matmul on the cycle-accurate leg needs minutes; see the
1026 `--step-timeout-ms` line in section 5.)
1027 
1028 This needs `<andesim/ROI.h>` markers inside llama.cpp, bounding ONE
1029 matvec-class operation (not a whole token) -- see `docs/llama_roi_howto.md`
1030 for the exact patch and how the insertion point was chosen. Since ggml
1031 builds its whole computation graph before executing it in one shot,
1032 individual operations are not distinguishable at the application call-site
1033 level (e.g. the per-layer forward-pass code) -- the markers go in ggml's
1034 own generic per-node dispatch loop instead, gated by a counter so only
1035 one specific node's execution is actually measured.
1036 
1037 Confirmed end to end (2026-07-16): the command above, targeting layer 7's
1038 V-projection matmul (the smallest matmul shape in this architecture --
1039 see `docs/llama_roi_howto.md` for how the target node was chosen and why
1040 the first, larger pick timed out even at 15 minutes), measured
1041 **6528953 cycles**, identical across two independent runs (this hart is
1042 deterministic single-hart, so a stable repeat cycle count is the
1043 correctness signal, the same contract the small matvec fixture above it
1044 already demonstrates). QEMU's hybrid leg enforces the real engine's
1045 ELEN=32 vector-unit limit (unlike fast mode's own unconstrained CPU
1046 string) -- getting a real llama.cpp build through it needed four small,
1047 targeted upstream fixes to `ggml/src/ggml-cpu/{vec.cpp,arch/riscv/quants.c}`,
1048 documented in `docs/llama_roi_howto.md` together with the exact
1049 `ANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K` value and the reasoning for picking it.
1050 
1051 Also confirmed on `vsim:ax46mpv_fpga_l3` (ELEN=64, VLEN=1024): the same
1052 K=51 node, **4476168 cycles**, with the PRISTINE upstream `ggml` source --
1053 none of the ELEN=32 fixes above are needed on this engine, since its real
1054 vector unit natively supports what those fixes route around. This engine
1055 needs a different, unrelated build-flag fix (its real ISA lacks Zcd,
1056 compressed double-FP load/store) and a much larger `--step-timeout-ms`
1057 (its cycle-accurate leg is far slower in wall-clock terms). See
1058 `docs/llama_roi_howto.md` section 8 for the exact recipe.

1 #!/usr/bin/env bash
   2 # Launch a Jupyter Lab server reachable from a remote browser.
   3 #
   4 # Usage:  scripts/notebook_server.sh [port]     (default: 8888)
   5 #
   6 # Needs only `uv` on the host: uvx downloads and caches JupyterLab on the
   7 # first run, so there is no permanent install. The server binds 0.0.0.0 with
   8 # auth disabled: anyone who can reach the port gets full access.
   9 set -euo pipefail
  10 
  11 PORT="${1:-${PORT:-8888}}"
  12 REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
  13 
  14 # This machine's LAN IP, for the URL a remote browser should use.
  15 IP="$(ip route get 1.1.1.1 2>/dev/null | awk '{for(i=1;i<NF;i++) if($i=="src") print $(i+1)}')"
  16 IP="${IP:-$(hostname -I 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $1}')}"
  17 
  18 echo "Open from a remote browser:"
  19 echo "  http://${IP}:${PORT}/lab"
  20 echo "Hybrid marker quickstart notebook directly:"
  21 echo "  http://${IP}:${PORT}/lab/tree/docs/hybrid_marker_quickstart.ipynb"
  22 echo
  23 
  24 exec uvx --from jupyterlab jupyter-lab \
  25     --ip 0.0.0.0 --port "$PORT" --no-browser \
  26     --IdentityProvider.token="" \
  27     --ServerApp.password="" \
  28     --notebook-dir "$REPO_ROOT"
=== config.env.example ===
   1 # Hybrid simulator per-host configuration.
   2 #
   3 # This file is the TEMPLATE (committed). On first `source ./setup.sh`,
   4 # it is copied to ./config.env (gitignored). Edit ./config.env to point
   5 # at the toolchain on your host; never commit your local edits.
   6 #
   7 # Precedence differs by consumer: setup.sh sources ./config.env
   8 # unconditionally, so the file's plain assignments overwrite any value
   9 # already exported in your shell. tests/lib/paths.sh sources it only
  10 # when HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN is unset, and the driver checks the environment
  11 # before parsing the file -- on those paths exported values can win.
  12 
  13 # Andes RISC-V GCC toolchain root (rv64). Must contain
  14 # bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-{gcc,ld,nm,objdump,...}.
  15 HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN=/local/nick/SW_Release/build-ast540/build-toolchain/linux/nds64le-elf-newlib-v5d
  16 
  17 # The rv32 toolchain root (separate install), for building rv32 runtime/fixtures.
  18 # Must contain bin/riscv32-unknown-elf-{gcc,ar,...}. Leave unset if you only
  19 # target rv64; rv32 runtime/fixture builds are skipped without it.
  20 HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32=/local/nick/SW_Release/build-ast540/build-toolchain/linux/nds32le-elf-newlib-v5d
  21 
  22 # Andes RISC-V glibc/Linux-ABI toolchain root (rv64), for building the
  23 # static-glibc test fixtures ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md U4+ needs (and
  24 # eventually llama-completion). Must contain bin/riscv64-linux-{gcc,g++,ld,...}.
  25 # Leave unset if you are not working on the vlinux Linux-runtime effort.
  26 LINUX_TOOLCHAIN=/local/nick/SW_Release/build-ast542/build-toolchain/linux/nds64le-linux-glibc-v5d
  27 
  28 # llama.cpp checkout root, ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md U8+. Needs a static
  29 # riscv64 build (see docs/USER_GUIDE.md section 11) at
  30 # $LLAMA_CPP_DIR/build-rv64-static/bin/llama-completion, and a GGUF model

   1 # Hybrid Simulator - Functional Requirements Specification
   2 
   3 Status: draft v0.1. Written 2026-05-29. Owner: Nick.
   4 Audience: Engineering, QA, IP/Legal, Sales engineering.
   5 
   6 Companion to `MRD.md` (commercial product view). This document is
   7 the **engineering contract**: every shippable behavior of Andes
   8 HybridSim v1.0, with one-line acceptance criteria per requirement.
   9 
  10 Requirement IDs are stable across drafts. Each FR traces back to
  11 one or more MR-x in MRD.md.
  12 
  13 ---
  14 
  15 ## 1. Scope and Definitions
  16 
  17 ### 1.1 In scope
  18 
  19 Andes HybridSim v1.0, the commercial Tier-2 hybrid simulator
  20 described in `MRD.md` sections 1-2. Specifically:
  21 
  22 - `hsim` driver CLI

########## docs/MRD.md ##########
   1 # Hybrid Simulator - Market Requirements Document
   2 
   3 Status: draft v1.0 (commercial rewrite). Written 2026-05-29.
   4 Owner: Nick. Audience: PM, BU lead, Sales engineering, Legal.
   5 
   6 Companion docs:
   7 - `FRS.md` - functional requirements specification (engineering contract)
   8 - `docs/USER_GUIDE.md` section 6 - current ROI envelope
   9 
  10 This document is the **product** view, written for a paying
  11 external buyer. The previous draft (v0.1) framed hybrid_sim as an
  12 Andes-internal acceleration tool. This rewrite repositions it as a
  13 commercial Tier-2 EDA product competing with ARM Cycle Models,
  14 Synopsys Imperas, and Wind River Simics-class hybrid offerings.
  15 
  16 ---
  17 
  18 ## 1. Executive Summary
  19 
  20 **Product name (working)**: Andes HybridSim
  21 **Category**: Cycle-accurate hybrid simulator for RISC-V SoCs
  22 **Cycle engine**: vsim (Verilator-derived, encrypted RTL pipeline)

########## docs/profile.md ##########
   1 # andesim profile - hot inner-loop detector
   2 
   3 Finds the hottest loops in a baremetal RISC-V ELF by observing backward
   4 translation-block transitions in QEMU. For each detected loop you get the
   5 loop header PC, the backward-branch PC, the iteration count, and a ready
   6 `measure: --pc-start .. --pc-end ..` window you can paste into a hybrid
   7 run. With DWARF, you also get the source `file:line`. With objdump
   8 present, you get RVV-only filtering and per-loop disassembly context.
   9 
  10 Two parts ship together:
  11 
  12 - `qemu_plugin/hotIterationLoop.c` - QEMU TCG plugin
  13   (`libhotIterationLoop.so`) that records edges.
  14 - `andesim profile` - the driver command that picks the engine, launches
  15   QEMU with the plugin, and formats the report.
  16 
  17 ## Usage
  18 
  19 ```
  20 ./andesim profile [--engine <id>] [options] <elf> [-- <extra qemu args>]
  21 ```
  22 

########## docs/engine_interface.md ##########
   1 # Engine interface
   2 
   3 How a simulator joins the `andesim` framework.
   4 
   5 `andesim` drives several simulator backends behind one CLI. An **engine** is
   6 one simulator *process* the framework can run: `qemu64`, `qemu32`, `vsim:ax45mpv_premium`,
   7 `vsim:ax66_makatau`, and -- if they implement this interface -- `alioth`,
   8 `sid`, or anything else. Engines are **drop-in binaries, not linked libraries**:
   9 the framework is never recompiled to add one. Everything `andesim` needs to
  10 know about an engine comes back from a single `--describe` call, so there is
  11 zero per-engine code in the framework.
  12 
  13 There is no separate engine-registration step, config-hash allowlist, or
  14 per-build CSR manifest requirement. Discovery uses the binary's descriptor;
  15 hybrid execution requires its accurate-leg interface and shared state ABI.
  16 
  17 To join, an engine does two things:
  18 
  19 1. **Self-describe** -- answer `--describe` with one JSON object (below).
  20 2. **Speak the ABI** for any role it claims that moves architectural state
  21    (`resume` / `drain`): read/write `struct hybrid_state_v1`
  22    (`include/hybrid/state_abi.h`) byte-for-byte. A functional-only engine that

########## docs/switching_modes_tutorial.md ##########
   1 # Switching-Mode Tutorial and Exercises
   2 
   3 Status: draft for review
   4 Audience: engineer running the hybrid simulator for the first time
   5 Scope: the 2 switching modes the repo ships, with copy-paste commands,
   6 the cycle figure each one yields, and one exercise per mode.
   7 
   8 ---
   9 
  10 ## 0. What "switching mode" means
  11 
  12 The hybrid simulator runs a program across two phases:
  13 
  14 ```
  15    QEMU1  --(state file + shared mmap)-->  vsim
  16    (fast)                                 (cycle accurate)
  17 ```
  18 
  19 A "switching mode" is the RULE that decides WHEN QEMU1 drains its
  20 architectural state and hands the region of interest to vsim. vsim runs
  21 that region cycle-accurately, then drains the final state. You pick
  22 the rule with plugin args and vsim CLI flags; the fixture binary does not

########## docs/llama_roi_howto.md ##########
   1 # Measuring one llama.cpp kernel iteration under andesim hybrid mode
   2 
   3 This is the companion doc USER_GUIDE.md section 11 points to: the exact
   4 patch that puts ROI markers around a matmul (or a short run of
   5 consecutive matmuls) inside llama.cpp, how the target was chosen, and
   6 the upstream `ggml` fixes a real build needs before it survives the
   7 cycle-accurate leg's ELEN=32 vector unit.
   8 
   9 Confirmed end to end:
  10 - 2026-07-16: single iteration (K=51, layer 7's V projection), on
  11   `vsim:ax45mpv_premium` (ELEN=32) -- **6528953 cycles**, stable across
  12   two independent hybrid runs.
  13 - 2026-07-16: two consecutive iterations (K=51..52, V then K
  14   projection), same engine -- **13040043 cycles** (~2x the
  15   single-iteration figure, as expected for two similarly-sized matmuls
  16   back to back). See section 6 for how to pick N.
  17 - 2026-07-16: single iteration (K=51), on `vsim:ax46mpv_fpga_l3`
  18   (ELEN=64, VLEN=1024, first engine with a real L3 cache) -- **4476168
  19   cycles**, with the PRISTINE upstream `ggml` source (none of section
  20   4's three ggml patches applied -- this engine's real ELEN=64 vector
  21   unit runs the original e64 code natively). Fewer cycles than
  22   ax45mpv_premium's for the SAME node: the doubled VLEN does more work

########## docs/hybrid_state_transport_problems.md ##########
   1 # Hybrid State Transport: CSR Problems and MMIO Problems
   2 
   3 ## Background (read this first)
   4 
   5 A hybrid run uses TWO simulators for ONE program:
   6 
   7 ```
   8   QEMU (fast, no timing)          vsim (slow, cycle-accurate)
   9   boot + setup code       ---->   the measured region (ROI)
  10                         "handoff"
  11 ```
  12 
  13 At the handoff we must make vsim's CPU look EXACTLY like QEMU's CPU at
  14 that moment. The copy has two steps:
  15 
  16 - **drain**: read all state out of QEMU into a file (`hybrid_state_v1`).
  17 - **restore**: write that file into the vsim hart through the Debug
  18   Module, then let it run.
  19 
  20 Two kinds of state travel, and their problems are different enough to
  21 list separately:
  22 

########## docs/csr_transport_ROADMAP.md ##########
   1 # ROADMAP: full Andes-V5 CSR transport coverage
   2 
   3 **Goal.** For the supported envelope - bare-metal, single-hart, **M-mode or
   4 M+U-mode**, trap-free ROI - verify the hybrid handoff correctly exchanges state
   5 for **every** CSR in `AndeStar_V5_SPA_UM164_V1.7`, with a per-section test and a
   6 machine-checked guarantee that nothing is missed.
   7 
   8 **Predecessor.** A now-retired Andes-CSR ROADMAP (RESOLVED) added the v3
   9 Andes block - 13 scalar CSRs + PMA - and the capability-gating flywheel. This
  10 ROADMAP reuses that exact pattern (one X-macro list, capability-gated, parity
  11 flywheel) to cover the remaining writable M-mode CSRs across the whole spec.
  12 
  13 ## The reality (why not "all 232 round-trip")
  14 
  15 The spec's Chapter 5 yields **232 CSR rows**. They split three ways (full table:
  16 `tests/andes_csr/csr_coverage.csv`):
  17 
  18 | group | count | what we do |
  19 |-------|-------|------------|
  20 | **carried today** | 41 | already round-trip through `hybrid_state_v1` |
  21 | **ADD** | 49 | writable M-mode plain state -> expand transport (this ROADMAP) |
  22 | **correctly excluded** | 142 | read-only config (29), RV32 shadows (21), side-effecting (11), N-ext (8), indirect-access (7), debug-internal (6), S/H mode-unsupported (57), other (3) |

########## ROADMAP.md ##########
   1 # Debug-Logging Roadmap: log levels -> reproducible bugs
   2 
   3 Goal: use the `--log-level` scale (0=trace 1=debug 2=info 3=warn 4=error
   4 5=critical 6=off, shared with vsim) so that any failed or suspicious run
   5 can be REPRODUCED and diagnosed from its own output, without re-running
   6 under ad-hoc printf debugging.
   7 
   8 Principles
   9 - info (default) stays clean: program output + the answer line. All new

1 #!/usr/bin/env bash
   2 # build_all.sh -- build the andesim artifacts. This is the entry point that
   3 # replaced the former `andesim build` subcommand (which moved out of the driver
   4 # binary). It only orchestrates the existing build scripts / Makefiles; the
   5 # build logic itself lives in setup.sh, scripts/build_*.sh, and the Makefiles.
   6 #
   7 # Usage:
   8 #   scripts/build_all.sh [TARGET] [--dry-run]
   9 #
  10 # TARGET (default: all):
  11 #   all       setup.sh (locate external qemu + vsim + plugin) then
  12 #             fixtures (the fixtures Makefile also builds the runtime lib too)
  13 #             then vlinux
  14 #   plugin    qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so
  15 #   fixtures  tests/fixtures/*.elf (+ runtime lib)
  16 #   runtime   build/runtime/ (rv64) + build/runtime/rv32/ (rv32, when
  17 #             HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32 is set): libandesim_runtime.a, crt0.o,
  18 #             andesim.ld, andesim.specs, include/andesim/ROI.h
  19 #   vlinux    build/runtime/linux/vlinux.elf (the vlinux proxy-kernel
  20 #             skeleton, ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md; depends on the runtime
  21 #             lib, built automatically)
  22 #
  23 # --dry-run prints the underlying commands without running them.
  24 #
  25 # The andesim driver itself is NOT built here: ./andesim self-bootstraps via
  26 # scripts/build_driver.sh on first use.
  27 set -euo pipefail
  28 
  29 ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
  30 
  31 TARGET=all
  32 DRY_RUN=0
  33 for arg in "$@"; do
  34   case "$arg" in
  35     --dry-run) DRY_RUN=1 ;;
  36     all|plugin|fixtures|runtime|vlinux) TARGET="$arg" ;;
  37     *)
  38       echo "build_all.sh: unknown argument: $arg" >&2
  39       echo "usage: build_all.sh [all|plugin|fixtures|runtime|vlinux] [--dry-run]" >&2
  40       exit 2
  41       ;;
  42   esac
  43 done
  44 
  45 # run one step: print it under --dry-run, otherwise banner + execute (inheriting
  46 # stdio so the user watches the build live). set -e aborts on the first failure.
  47 run() {
  48   if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "1" ]; then
  49     printf '%s\n' "$*"
  50     return
  51   fi
  52   printf '[build_all] %s\n' "$*"
  53   "$@"
  54 }
  55 
  56 # plugin: build_qemu_plugin.sh wraps `make -C qemu_plugin`; plugins build against
  57 # the vendored qemu_plugin/include/qemu-plugin.h (no QEMU source tree needed).
  58 case "$TARGET" in
  59   all)      run bash "$ROOT/setup.sh"; run make -C "$ROOT/tests/fixtures"; run make -C "$ROOT/runtime/linux" ;;
  60   plugin)   run bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_qemu_plugin.sh" ;;
  61   fixtures) run make -C "$ROOT/tests/fixtures" ;;
  62   runtime)  run bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_runtime.sh" ;;
  63   vlinux)   run make -C "$ROOT/runtime/linux" ;;
  64 esac
=== Dockerfile.runtime ===
   1 # andesim runtime image -- for run-only hosts (macOS via podman machine).
   2 #
   3 # Built ON LINUX (CI or a Linux workstation); macOS users only pull it:
   4 #
   5 #   podman build -f Dockerfile.runtime \
   6 #     --build-arg BASE_IMAGE=<verilator env image> \
   7 #     -t andesim-runtime:latest .
   8 #
   9 # BASE_IMAGE is the vsim build environment from the external vsim repo's
  10 # root Dockerfile (target `env`) -- the same image its build_vsim.sh builds
  11 # (vsim-env:latest), so the Verilator/SystemC toolchain and QEMU build deps
  12 # are already there.
  13 # The publish registry/name is still an open question; consumers override
  14 # the local default with ANDESIM_IMAGE.
  15 #
  16 # The whole repo is baked, fully built, at /opt/hybrid_sim, so the baked
  17 # ./andesim resolves every artifact via its normal repo-relative paths
  18 # (plugin, runtime). scripts/run_in_container.sh
  19 # invokes that path as the entry; the user's cwd is bind-mounted only for
  20 # ELF inputs and outputs.
  21 ARG BASE_IMAGE=andes-vsim-env:latest
  22 FROM ${BASE_IMAGE}
  23 
  24 COPY . /opt/hybrid_sim
  25 WORKDIR /opt/hybrid_sim
  26 
  27 # Build: plugin -> driver -> runtime. Both QEMU and vsim are NOT built here --
  28 # they are integrated as external prebuilt binaries; provide them at run time, e.g.
  29 #   -v /path/to/qemu/build:/qemu:ro   -e VSIM_QEMU=/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64
  30 #   -v /path/to/vsim/build:/vsim:ro   -e VSIM_BIN_DIR=/vsim
  31 # (the plugin builds against the vendored qemu_plugin/include/qemu-plugin.h, so
  32 # no QEMU source tree is needed; the driver discovers cycle engines by scanning
  33 # $VSIM_BIN_DIR). setup.sh is NOT used here -- it locates the external qemu/vsim,
  34 # which are mounted at run time, not build time.
  35 RUN make -C qemu_plugin \
  36  && ./scripts/build_driver.sh \
  37  && make -C runtime
  38 
  39 ENTRYPOINT ["/opt/hybrid_sim/andesim"]
=== run_in_container.sh ===
   1 #!/usr/bin/env bash
   2 # Run andesim inside the prebuilt Linux runtime image -- the macOS path
   3 # (see Dockerfile.runtime; macOS is run-only, builds happen on Linux CI).
   4 #
   5 # Two rules make the hybrid handoff correct across the podman-machine VM:
   6 #   1. The shared mmap stays VM-local: the container's /dev/shm (--shm-size)
   7 #      is tier 1, and the host's HSIM_MMAP_DIR is never forwarded -- a host
   8 #      path would be a virtiofs mount, where MAP_SHARED is not coherent.
   9 #   2. The caller's cwd is bind-mounted at the SAME path, so relative ELF
  10 #      arguments and output files behave as if the run were local (plain
  11 #      file IO is fine across the boundary; only the mmap is not).
  12 set -euo pipefail
  13 
  14 ENGINE="${ANDESIM_CONTAINER_ENGINE:-}"
  15 if [ -z "$ENGINE" ]; then
  16   if command -v podman >/dev/null 2>&1; then ENGINE=podman
  17   elif command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1; then ENGINE=docker
  18   else
  19     echo "andesim: a macOS run executes inside a Linux VM and needs podman (or docker)" >&2
  20     echo "           install podman and run: podman machine init && podman machine start" >&2
  21     exit 2
  22   fi
  23 fi
  24 
  25 IMAGE="${ANDESIM_IMAGE:-andesim-runtime:latest}"
  26 SHM_SIZE="${ANDESIM_SHM_SIZE:-3g}"   # tier 1 ceiling inside the VM
  27 ENTRY="${ANDESIM_IMAGE_ENTRY:-/opt/hybrid_sim/andesim}"
  28 
  29 TTY_ARGS=()
  30 if [ -t 0 ] && [ -t 1 ]; then TTY_ARGS=(-it); fi
  31 
  32 exec "$ENGINE" run --rm "${TTY_ARGS[@]}" \
  33   --shm-size "$SHM_SIZE" \
  34   -v "$PWD:$PWD" \
  35   -w "$PWD" \
  36   "$IMAGE" "$ENTRY" "$@"

   1 #!/usr/bin/env bash
   2 # Run andesim inside the prebuilt Linux runtime image -- the macOS path
   3 # (see Dockerfile.runtime; macOS is run-only, builds happen on Linux CI).
   4 #
   5 # Two rules make the hybrid handoff correct across the podman-machine VM:
   6 #   1. The shared mmap stays VM-local: the container's /dev/shm (--shm-size)
   7 #      is tier 1, and the host's HSIM_MMAP_DIR is never forwarded -- a host
   8 #      path would be a virtiofs mount, where MAP_SHARED is not coherent.
   9 #   2. The caller's cwd is bind-mounted at the SAME path, so relative ELF
  10 #      arguments and output files behave as if the run were local (plain
  11 #      file IO is fine across the boundary; only the mmap is not).
  12 set -euo pipefail
  13 
  14 ENGINE="${ANDESIM_CONTAINER_ENGINE:-}"
  15 if [ -z "$ENGINE" ]; then
  16   if command -v podman >/dev/null 2>&1; then ENGINE=podman
  17   elif command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1; then ENGINE=docker
  18   else
  19     echo "andesim: a macOS run executes inside a Linux VM and needs podman (or docker)" >&2
  20     echo "           install podman and run: podman machine init && podman machine start" >&2
  21     exit 2
  22   fi
  23 fi
  24 
  25 IMAGE="${ANDESIM_IMAGE:-andesim-runtime:latest}"
  26 SHM_SIZE="${ANDESIM_SHM_SIZE:-3g}"   # tier 1 ceiling inside the VM
  27 ENTRY="${ANDESIM_IMAGE_ENTRY:-/opt/hybrid_sim/andesim}"
  28 
  29 TTY_ARGS=()
  30 if [ -t 0 ] && [ -t 1 ]; then TTY_ARGS=(-it); fi
  31 
  32 exec "$ENGINE" run --rm "${TTY_ARGS[@]}" \
  33   --shm-size "$SHM_SIZE" \
  34   -v "$PWD:$PWD" \
  35   -w "$PWD" \
  36   "$IMAGE" "$ENTRY" "$@"

1 #!/usr/bin/env bash
   2 # test_all.sh -- run the full andesim test surface. This is the entry point that
   3 # replaced the former `andesim test` subcommand (which moved out of the binary).
   4 #
   5 # Phases (all run, in order, unless named explicitly):
   6 #   lint      tests/test_*.sh + roi.test.sh + the fixture ROI-content lint
   7 #             (fast harness self-checks; no engine spawns. The one heavy
   8 #             harness test, tests/test_kernel_cycles.sh, stays manual: it
   9 #             runs real QEMU+vsim round-trips the e2e phase already covers.)
  10 #   unit      build/driver/andesim-*-test   the C++ driver unit tests
  11 #   contract  tests/andes_sim/*.sh          driver feature + parity contracts
  12 #   e2e       scripts/run_e2e.sh            hybrid qemu+vsim round-trips
  13 #
  14 # Usage:
  15 #   scripts/test_all.sh [--dry-run] [lint|unit|contract|e2e ...]
  16 #
  17 # --dry-run prints the plan without executing (and without building). The
  18 # contract and e2e phases need built artifacts -- run scripts/build_all.sh
  19 # first. FILTER / MODE / JOBS pass through to scripts/run_e2e.sh unchanged.
  20 set -uo pipefail
  21 
  22 ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
  23 
  24 DRY_RUN=0
  25 PHASES=()
  26 for arg in "$@"; do
  27   case "$arg" in
  28     --dry-run) DRY_RUN=1 ;;
  29     lint|unit|contract|e2e) PHASES+=("$arg") ;;
  30     *)
  31       echo "test_all.sh: unknown argument: $arg" >&2
  32       echo "usage: test_all.sh [--dry-run] [lint|unit|contract|e2e ...]" >&2
  33       exit 2
  34       ;;
  35   esac
  36 done
  37 [ "${#PHASES[@]}" -eq 0 ] && PHASES=(lint unit contract e2e)
  38 
  39 step() { printf '\033[1;34m==>\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
  40 ok()   { printf '\033[1;32m[ok]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
  41 fail() { printf '\033[1;31m[FAIL]\033[0m %s\n' "$*" >&2; }
  42 
  43 pass=0
  44 failed=0
  45 declare -a FAILED_NAMES=()

   1 #!/usr/bin/env bash
   2 # Run the confirmed llama.cpp hybrid example from docs/llama_roi_howto.md
   3 # (section 5): layer 7's V projection (K=51) on vsim:ax45mpv_premium.
   4 # Expected: [andesim] 6528953 cycles, ~13 min wall clock.
   5 #
   6 # Usage:
   7 #   scripts/run_llama_hybrid.sh            # run (uses existing build)
   8 #   BUILD=1 scripts/run_llama_hybrid.sh    # reconfigure + rebuild, then run
   9 #   ROI_K=52 BUILD=1 scripts/run_llama_hybrid.sh   # retarget the measured node
  10 set -euo pipefail
  11 
  12 ANDESIM_DIR="${ANDESIM_DIR:-$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)}"
  13 LLAMA_DIR="${LLAMA_DIR:-/home/nick/work/llama.cpp}"
  14 BUILD_DIR="$LLAMA_DIR/build-rv64-static"
  15 MODEL="${MODEL:-$LLAMA_DIR/models/Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf}"
  16 ENGINE="${ENGINE:-vsim:ax45mpv_premium}"
  17 ROI_K="${ROI_K:-51}"
  18 KANATA="${KANATA:-}"   # set to a path to also dump a Kanata pipeline trace
  19 
  20 if [[ "${BUILD:-0}" == 1 ]]; then
  21     FLAGS="-mext-zvlsseg -DANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K=$ROI_K -I $ANDESIM_DIR/build/runtime/include"
  22     cmake -B "$BUILD_DIR" -S "$LLAMA_DIR" \
  23         -DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS=OFF -DGGML_NATIVE=OFF -DGGML_OPENMP=OFF \
  24         -DGGML_RV_ZFH=OFF -DGGML_RV_ZVFH=OFF -DGGML_CPU_REPACK=OFF \
  25         -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS="$FLAGS" -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS="$FLAGS"
  26     cmake --build "$BUILD_DIR" -j --target llama-completion
  27     # doc section 3: confirm the .o really carries the intended K
  28     python3 -c "
  29 import json
  30 for e in json.load(open('$BUILD_DIR/compile_commands.json')):
  31     if e['file'].endswith('ggml-cpu.c'):
  32         print(e['command']); break
  33 " | grep -o "ANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K=$ROI_K" \
  34         || { echo "ERROR: ggml-cpu.c not configured with K=$ROI_K" >&2; exit 1; }
  35 fi
  36 
  37 [[ -x "$BUILD_DIR/bin/llama-completion" ]] \
  38     || { echo "ERROR: $BUILD_DIR/bin/llama-completion missing; rerun with BUILD=1" >&2; exit 1; }
  39 [[ -f "$MODEL" ]] || { echo "ERROR: model $MODEL missing" >&2; exit 1; }

--- cell 0 [markdown] ---
# andesim quickstart: hybrid mode with the marker trigger

This notebook runs real `./andesim` commands and shows their real output.
It covers the simplest measuring flow:

1. Check the install.
2. Run a prebuilt ELF in hybrid mode with `--trigger marker`.
3. Write, compile, and measure your own C program with ROI markers.
4. Preview a run with `--dry-run`.

**What hybrid mode does:** QEMU (fast, functional) runs your program until
the ROI start marker. Then it hands the full CPU state and memory to the
cycle-accurate engine (vsim, built from real RTL), which runs only your
region-of-interest (ROI) and reports how many cycles it took.

**Prerequisites:** a built andesim install (see `README.md`). Run this
notebook from the repo (it lives in `docs/`; the first cell moves to the
repo root). You can serve it with `scripts/notebook_server.sh`.


--- cell 1 [code] ---
# Move to the repo root (the notebook lives in docs/).
import os
if not os.path.exists("./andesim"):
    %cd ..
assert os.path.exists("./andesim"), "run this notebook from the andesim repo"
print("repo root:", os.getcwd())

--- cell 2 [markdown] ---
## Step 1: check the install

`./andesim doctor` is a read-only health report. A healthy install ends
with `0 FAIL`. It also lists the engines and where the shared memory for
hybrid runs will live (`mmap tiers`).


--- cell 3 [code] ---
!./andesim doctor

--- cell 4 [markdown] ---
`./andesim list engines` shows what `--engine` accepts. Hybrid mode needs
one `vsim:` (cycle-accurate) engine. With more than one installed, you
must pick one with `--engine`.


--- cell 5 [code] ---
!./andesim list engines

--- cell 6 [markdown] ---
## Step 2: first hybrid run with a prebuilt ELF

The install ships ready-made test ELFs under `tests/fixtures/`.
`rt_c_hello.elf` already contains ROI markers, so `--trigger marker`
works out of the box.

The command has three required parts:

- `--mode hybrid` picks the model.
- `--trigger marker` says the ROI is the span between the markers in the
  binary.
- `--engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium` picks the cycle-accurate engine.

(`run` is the default command, so you may also drop the word `run`:
`./andesim --mode hybrid ...` works the same.)


--- cell 7 [code] ---
!./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker \
    --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf

--- cell 8 [markdown] ---
How to read the output:

- `hello from QEMU1` is the program's own output from the fast leg.
- `[andesim] N cycles` is the answer: the ROI took N cycles on this
  engine. It is the vsim `mcycle` delta across the window.
- The run ends after the ROI. Code after the end marker never executes:
  hybrid is a measuring tool, not a way to finish the program.

Note: the FIRST hybrid run of a given (engine, ELF) pair is a few seconds
slower. andesim captures the engine's reset state once and caches it under
`~/.cache/andesim/`, so later runs skip restoring registers that still
hold reset values. This never changes results.

By default (`--log-level 2`, info) andesim prints only your program's
output and the cycle figure. `--log-level 1` (debug, same scale as the
vsim engines: 0=trace .. 6=off) adds the driver's chatter -- the resolved
engine banner, the shared-memory (`[andesim] mmap`) line, and

--- cell 9 [code] ---
!./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker \
    --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium --log-level 1 tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf

--- cell 10 [markdown] ---
## Step 3: measure your own program

Wrap the region you want to measure with the two ROI markers from
`<andesim/ROI.h>` (shipped with the runtime):

```c
#include <andesim/ROI.h>

andesim_ROI_begin();
my_kernel(a, b, c);
andesim_ROI_end();
```

The markers are RISC-V HINT instructions (architectural NOPs), so the
same binary also runs unchanged on `fast`, on `cycle`, and on real
silicon.

Measurement hygiene: keep the kernel in a `__attribute__((noinline))`
function called between the markers, and pass inputs/outputs through
memory. This stops the compiler from moving your compute out of the
measured window.

--- cell 0 [markdown] ---
# andesim quickstart: hybrid mode with the marker trigger

This notebook runs real `./andesim` commands and shows their real output.
It covers the simplest measuring flow:

1. Check the install.
2. Run a prebuilt ELF in hybrid mode with `--trigger marker`.
3. Write, compile, and measure your own C program with ROI markers.
4. Preview a run with `--dry-run`.

**What hybrid mode does:** QEMU (fast, functional) runs your program until
the ROI start marker. Then it hands the full CPU state and memory to the
cycle-accurate engine (vsim, built from real RTL), which runs only your
region-of-interest (ROI) and reports how many cycles it took.

**Prerequisites:** a built andesim install (see `README.md`). Run this
notebook from the repo (it lives in `docs/`; the first cell moves to the
repo root). You can serve it with `scripts/notebook_server.sh`.


--- cell 1 [code] ---
# Move to the repo root (the notebook lives in docs/).
import os
if not os.path.exists("./andesim"):
    %cd ..
assert os.path.exists("./andesim"), "run this notebook from the andesim repo"
print("repo root:", os.getcwd())

--- cell 2 [markdown] ---
## Step 1: check the install

`./andesim doctor` is a read-only health report. A healthy install ends
with `0 FAIL`. It also lists the engines and where the shared memory for
hybrid runs will live (`mmap tiers`).


--- cell 3 [code] ---
!./andesim doctor

--- cell 4 [markdown] ---
`./andesim list engines` shows what `--engine` accepts. Hybrid mode needs
one `vsim:` (cycle-accurate) engine. With more than one installed, you
must pick one with `--engine`.


--- cell 5 [code] ---
!./andesim list engines

--- cell 6 [markdown] ---
## Step 2: first hybrid run with a prebuilt ELF

The install ships ready-made test ELFs under `tests/fixtures/`.
`rt_c_hello.elf` already contains ROI markers, so `--trigger marker`
works out of the box.

The command has three required parts:

- `--mode hybrid` picks the model.
- `--trigger marker` says the ROI is the span between the markers in the
  binary.
- `--engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium` picks the cycle-accurate engine.

(`run` is the default command, so you may also drop the word `run`:
`./andesim --mode hybrid ...` works the same.)


--- cell 7 [code] ---
!./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker \
    --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf

--- cell 8 [markdown] ---
How to read the output:

- `hello from QEMU1` is the program's own output from the fast leg.
- `[andesim] N cycles` is the answer: the ROI took N cycles on this
  engine. It is the vsim `mcycle` delta across the window.
- The run ends after the ROI. Code after the end marker never executes:
  hybrid is a measuring tool, not a way to finish the program.

Note: the FIRST hybrid run of a given (engine, ELF) pair is a few seconds
slower. andesim captures the engine's reset state once and caches it under
`~/.cache/andesim/`, so later runs skip restoring registers that still
hold reset values. This never changes results.

By default (`--log-level 2`, info) andesim prints only your program's
output and the cycle figure. `--log-level 1` (debug, same scale as the
vsim engines: 0=trace .. 6=off) adds the driver's chatter -- the resolved
engine banner, the shared-memory (`[andesim] mmap`) line, and

--- cell 9 [code] ---
!./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker \
    --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium --log-level 1 tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf

--- cell 10 [markdown] ---
## Step 3: measure your own program

Wrap the region you want to measure with the two ROI markers from
`<andesim/ROI.h>` (shipped with the runtime):

```c
#include <andesim/ROI.h>

andesim_ROI_begin();
my_kernel(a, b, c);
andesim_ROI_end();
```

The markers are RISC-V HINT instructions (architectural NOPs), so the
same binary also runs unchanged on `fast`, on `cycle`, and on real
silicon.

Measurement hygiene: keep the kernel in a `__attribute__((noinline))`
function called between the markers, and pass inputs/outputs through
memory. This stops the compiler from moving your compute out of the
measured window.

142	 1. The built-in `qemu64` (rv64) and `qemu32` (rv32) descriptors are always
143	 present (QEMU does not implement `--describe`; their binary paths honor
144	 `$VSIM_QEMU` / `$VSIM_QEMU32`, then `$QEMU_BIN_DIR`).
145	 2. The scan directory is:
146	 - `$ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR` if set (colon-separated; **replaces** the default
147	 and accepts **any** executable -- this is where you drop `alioth` / `sid`),
148	 - otherwise `$VSIM_BIN_DIR` (the external prebuilt vsim build dir, mirroring
149	 `$QEMU_BIN_DIR`; falls back to the legacy in-tree `<repo>/verilator/build`
150	 when unset), filtered to `sim_*` binaries.
151	 3. For each candidate binary the framework runs `<bin> --describe`. If that
152	 fails (non-zero, hang past a 5 s timeout, or non-JSON) it falls back to a
153	 sidecar file `<bin>.json` containing the same descriptor -- the escape hatch
154	 for binaries that cannot add the flag.
155	 4. Descriptors are deduped by `id`.
156	
157	 Because discovery is pure runtime scan + self-describe, **building a new
158	 Verilator config and dropping `sim_<cfg>` into the scan dir makes it appear with
159	 no `andesim` rebuild.** That is the hot-plug guarantee.
160	
161	 ## Joining as a new engine (alioth / sid)
162	
163	 1. Implement `--describe` to print the JSON above (set `id`, `type`, `kind`,
164	 the roles you support, and `invoke` templates for those roles). If you cannot
165	 add the flag, ship a `<bin>.json` sidecar instead.
166	 2. If you claim `resume`/`drain`, read/write `hybrid_state_v1` per
167	 `include/hybrid/state_abi.h`.
168	 3. Put the binary on `$ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR` and run `andesim list engines`
169	 to confirm it shows up. Done -- no framework change required.
170	 4. **(Optional) GDB support**: `andesim run --mode cycle --gdb [--gdb-port N]` injects `--jtag-port <N>` (default 9104) into the engine argv before the user passthrough, then exec-replaces itself with ICEman (`$ICEMAN`). If your engine supports a JTAG bitbang port, implement `--jtag-port` to match vsim's interface. If it does not, the framework still builds the argv correctly -- the engine will simply ignore or reject the flag.
171	 5. **(Optional) QEMU ISA match**: implement `--print-qemu-config` to emit a QEMU `-readconfig` cfg (per-extension `[global]` properties) describing your engine's ISA, so a hybrid run's QEMU fast leg executes the same extensions you model. On a hybrid run the framework runs `<accurate-engine> --print-qemu-config` and passes the result to QEMU via `-readconfig`. If you do not implement it (the flag exits non-zero), the framework falls back to QEMU's default `-cpu` -- no error. vsim bakes this cfg from its `config.inc` at build time.

---

# AndeSim Documentation Audit — Release Readiness for a First-Time External User

## 0. Top-line finding (blocking)

**Every documentation file in the repo is deleted in the working tree.** `git status` shows all 14 tracked `.md`/`.ipynb` docs as ` D` (deleted, unstaged). `/home/nick/work/andesim/docs/` does not exist on disk. A release package tarred from the working tree today would ship **zero documentation** — no README, no user guide, no notebook — while `README.md` and `USER_GUIDE.md` cross-reference each other and `./andesim doctor`'s own error text points users at `README.md`.

Also missing entirely from the tracked set: **no LICENSE, no COPYING, no NOTICE, no CHANGELOG, no INSTALL guide, no CONTRIBUTING**. `docs/FRS.md:521-530` (FR-705) itself lists "Installation guide", "ABI reference", "Integration guide", "Limitations document", "Error code reference", "Release notes" as required shipped docs — **none of these exist**.

---

## 1. Doc inventory: size, audience, classification

| File | Lines | Bytes | Stated / inferred audience | Classification |
|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| `README.md` | 48 | 1,772 | Whoever clones the repo | **User-facing** (build/install entry point) — but written for an internal cloner, not a package recipient |
| `docs/USER_GUIDE.md` | 1,058 | 48,872 | `:3` "an engineer who wants to RUN programs on the Andes simulators" | **User-facing product doc** — the only real one. High quality. |
| `docs/profile.md` | 285 | 11,760 | Users of `andesim profile` | **User-facing** (reference for one command) |
| `docs/engine_interface.md` | 171 | 10,053 | `:3` "How a simulator joins the andesim framework"; USER_GUIDE:829 calls it "for engine vendors/integrators, not needed to run workloads" | **User-facing (partner/integrator tier)**, not end-user |
| `docs/switching_modes_tutorial.md` | 324 | 12,852 | `:3-4` "Status: draft for review / Audience: engineer running the hybrid simulator for the first time" | **Intended user-facing, but STALE** — see §2. Contains 3 hardcoded `/home/nick` paths and the retired repo name `hybrid_sim`. |
| `docs/hybrid_marker_quickstart.ipynb` | 593 | 20,733 | First-time user, runnable notebook | **User-facing tutorial** — but its *captured outputs* leak the author's machine wholesale (10+ `/home/nick/...` strings) |
| `docs/llama_roi_howto.md` | 365 | 18,580 | Someone reproducing the llama.cpp ROI measurement | **Hybrid**: a real how-to, but reads as an engineering lab notebook (dated confirmations, per-engine caveats, upstream patch diffs) |
| `docs/MRD.md` | 410 | 15,599 | `:4` "Owner: Nick. Audience: PM, BU lead, Sales engineering, Legal" | **Internal — commercially sensitive.** Contains price bands ($20K–200K/seat/yr), competitor teardowns, revenue model, license-enforcement design, risk register. **Must not ship.** |
| `docs/FRS.md` | 687 | 22,171 | `:3-4` "Owner: Nick. Audience: Engineering, QA, IP/Legal, Sales engineering" | **Internal** engineering contract / requirements spec (`Status: draft v0.1`). Must not ship. |
| `docs/hybrid_state_transport_problems.md` | 350 | 16,547 | Implementers of the state transport | **Internal dev notes** (problem/status/fix matrices, OPEN items) |
| `docs/csr_transport_ROADMAP.md` | 121 | 7,345 | Transport implementers | **Internal roadmap** |
| `ROADMAP.md` | 145 | 6,805 | Self ("Rollout: one feature per session, TDD-first", `:136`) | **Internal roadmap** |
| `ROADMAP_HTIF_WINDOW.md` | 102 | 4,924 | Self; references cross-repo file paths | **Internal roadmap** |
| `ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md` | 1,414 | 88,849 | Self; the largest file in the repo | **Internal roadmap** — 6 `/home/nick` paths, internal toolchain build IDs |
| `REFACTOR_ROADMAP.md` | 145 | 7,543 | Self; "93-agent review", "scratchpad discovery.json (session 6e8f04a6)" | **Internal roadmap** |
| `CLAUDE.md` (also tracked, not in your list) | 207 | 23,791 | Claude Code agent instructions | **Internal tooling config** — should not ship |

**Ratio: ~2,500 lines of user-facing doc vs ~3,400 lines of internal roadmap/PM material, all in the same tree with no separation mechanism** (no `docs/internal/`, no packaging manifest, no `.gitattributes export-ignore`).

---

## 2. README + USER_GUIDE: the actual first-run flow, and where it breaks

### What the docs say the flow is

`README.md:16-22` — the entire documented install:
```
git clone --recursive https://gitea.andestech.com/nick/hybrid_sim && cd hybrid_sim
bash scripts/build_all.sh
bash scripts/test_all.sh
```
`README.md:30-39` — host deps: C/C++ toolchain (clang preferred), CMake ≥3.20, ninja, Python 3, glib-2.0 dev, pkg-config, a prebuilt `qemu-system-riscv64`, a prebuilt vsim.

`docs/USER_GUIDE.md:7-11` explicitly refuses to cover install: *"It assumes andesim and its engines are already installed and built... building is covered in `README.md`, not here."* Then §2 (`:38-74`) → `./andesim doctor`, `list models`, `list engines`; §3 (`:77-143`) → three first runs against `tests/fixtures/*.elf`.

### Concrete gaps

**G1 — The quickstart cannot work for an external user; it fails on step 2.**
`scripts/build_all.sh all` runs `setup.sh` (`scripts/build_all.sh:59`). `setup.sh:67-84` copies `config.env.example` → `config.env`, sources it, then hard-fails:
- `setup.sh:81` `[ ! -d "$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin" ]` → dies, because the template value is `config.env.example:15` `HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN=/local/nick/SW_Release/build-ast540/build-toolchain/linux/nds64le-elf-newlib-v5d`.
- Then `setup.sh:89-98` requires `QEMU_BIN_DIR` with **both** `qemu-system-riscv32` **and** `qemu-system-riscv64`; template default `config.env.example:41` = `/home/nick/work/qemu_andesim/build/qemu`.
- Then `setup.sh:102-109` requires `sim_*` under `VSIM_BIN_DIR`; template default `config.env.example:47` = `/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/build`.

**README never mentions `config.env` in the quickstart at all.** It is mentioned only afterwards, in the "Host dependencies" and "Outputs" prose (`README.md:12-14, 36-39, 47-48`). There is no "edit config.env first" step. Result: a first-time user's literal first command sequence dies with `HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN=/local/nick/... has no bin/ directory`.

**G2 — The clone URL is an internal Gitea host.** `README.md:19` `https://gitea.andestech.com/nick/hybrid_sim`. An external user has no access, and the repo name (`hybrid_sim`) no longer matches the product (`andesim`).

**G3 — The `include/` submodule is also internal-only and is required.** `.gitmodules:3` `url = https://gitea.andestech.com/nick/andesim_abi.git`. `--recursive` clone fails for anyone outside the network; `README.md:9-11` and `CLAUDE.md:10-13` both state `include/hybrid/state_abi.h` is the shared ABI required by the plugin, driver, and vsim. A release tarball must vendor it — nothing documents that.

**G4 — Nothing tells the user how to obtain QEMU or vsim.** README says both are "prebuilt external binaries" and that "vsim sources live in the separate `hybrid_vsim` repo, built there" (`README.md:12-14`) — **with no URL, no download link, no version/ABI requirement, no build instructions**. `CLAUDE.md:17-21` says the same, adding the sources moved to `hybrid_vsim` with its own `build_vsim.sh`. Circular: README defers to a repo the user cannot find. Same for the RISC-V toolchain: `README.md` never lists it as a host dependency at all, yet `setup.sh:77-84` hard-requires `HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN` before doing anything.

**G5 — Missing prerequisites in README's host-deps list** (all provably required by tracked code, none listed at `README.md:30-39`):
- Andes RISC-V bare-metal GCC (`HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN`) — required by `setup.sh:77`; mentioned only in `USER_GUIDE.md:159` as "your Andes RISC-V GCC".
- Andes rv32 GCC (`HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32`) — needed for rv32 runtime/fixtures (`scripts/build_all.sh:16-18`); documented only in `config.env.example:17-20`.
- Andes static-glibc Linux toolchain (`LINUX_TOOLCHAIN`) — required by `--runtime linux`'s `objcopy` step (`USER_GUIDE.md:600-601`), not in README.
- `make`, `bash` — implicit.
- `podman`/`docker` for macOS (`USER_GUIDE.md:783-796`).
- `uv`/`uvx` for the notebook (`scripts/notebook_server.sh:6`).
- `python3` is listed, but its actual uses (`scripts/classify_csr_coverage.py`, `tests/andes_csr/check_coverage.py`, `scripts/run_llama_hybrid.sh:28`) are undocumented.

**G6 — README's "Outputs" section is incomplete.** `README.md:43-48` claims `build_all.sh` produces only the two `.so` plugins. It omits `build/andesim` (the driver — actually self-bootstrapped by `./andesim:18`), `build/runtime/` (the `.a`, `crt0.o`, `andesim.ld`, `andesim.specs`, `include/andesim/ROI.h` — all of which `USER_GUIDE.md:154-196` tells the user to link against), `tests/fixtures/*.elf`, and `build/runtime/linux/vlinux.elf`.

**G7 — macOS setup is a dead end.** `USER_GUIDE.md:787` literally says `podman pull <runtime image>      # or load a CI-built andesim-runtime:latest` — an unresolved placeholder. `Dockerfile.runtime:13-14` confirms: *"The publish registry/name is still an open question."* No registry, no image, no CI reference an external user can act on.

**G8 — Undocumented flags and env vars.**
- `--mmap-size` — accepted by `driver/cli.cpp:109` (aliased to `--mem-size`, "retired spelling"). Appears in **no** doc and no `--help` output. A user who finds it in an old script gets silent aliasing.
- `--runtime <linux>` — parsed at `driver/cli.cpp:110`, fully documented in `USER_GUIDE.md:587-670`, but **absent from the `--help` option table** (`driver/main.cpp:72-90`, `kRunOpts`). It only appears obliquely inside the `-- <args...>` line at `driver/main.cpp:89`.
- `--print-qemu-config` — an engine-facing flag documented in `docs/profile.md` and `docs/engine_interface.md:171`; fine, but not in USER_GUIDE's engine section.
- `ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR` — documented **only** in `docs/engine_interface.md:146-147`. It is a real user knob (it *replaces* the default scan dir and accepts any executable) and is absent from `USER_GUIDE.md`, `README.md`, and `config.env.example`.
- `ANDESIM_DEV` — read by the driver (`driver/dev_mode.hpp` / `driver/main.cpp:52-62`, exposes the `fixtures` list target); documented nowhere.
- `VSIM_PLUGIN`, `ANDESIM_OS`, `ANDESIM_IMAGE_ENTRY` — read by code (`driver`, `./andesim:13`, `scripts/run_in_container.sh:27`), documented in no user doc.
- `QEMU_BIN_DIR` / `VSIM_QEMU` / `VSIM_QEMU32` — never mentioned in `USER_GUIDE.md` at all (README + `config.env.example` only).

**G9 — Stale cross-references.** `docs/MRD.md:8` and `docs/FRS.md:528` both cite *"`docs/USER_GUIDE.md` section 6 — current ROI envelope"*. In the current guide, §6 is the `profile` command (`USER_GUIDE.md:674`); the ROI envelope is §7 (`USER_GUIDE.md:750`).

**G10 — Product-name inconsistency across the doc set.** `README.md:1` titles the project `# hybrid_sim`. `docs/FRS.md` calls the CLI `hsim` **20 times** (e.g. `FRS.md:22`, `FRS.md:518`); `docs/MRD.md:44` also says `hsim` — while the actual binary is `andesim` and MRD brands the product "Andes HybridSim" (`MRD.md:20`). `Dockerfile.runtime:24` and `scripts/run_in_container.sh:27` bake `/opt/hybrid_sim`. ## 4. Does any doc explain what the user provides vs what ships?

**Partially, and inconsistently — no single authoritative statement exists.**

What exists:

- `README.md:12-14, 36-39, 47-48` — the clearest statement: QEMU and vsim are "prebuilt external binaries", set `QEMU_BIN_DIR`/`VSIM_BIN_DIR`; "this repo no longer builds QEMU"; "vsim sources live in the separate `hybrid_vsim` repo, built there." **But no source, no URL, no version constraint, no ABI-compatibility statement, and the toolchain is not mentioned as a user-supplied item at all.**
- `config.env.example:13-47` — the best per-item description (what each of the 6 external things is, what must be inside it, and that some are optional). It is a config template, not a doc, and is not linked from README's quickstart.
- `setup.sh:88-110` — enforces it at runtime with decent error messages ("build both rv32+rv64 QEMU there or edit `$CONFIG_FILE`").
- `CLAUDE.md:15-21` — accurate, but this is agent-instruction internal.
- `docs/USER_GUIDE.md:7-11` — **explicitly declines** to cover it and defers to README.
- `docs/USER_GUIDE.md:159` — "Use your Andes RISC-V GCC (the one `./andesim doctor` reports)" — the only user-facing hint that the toolchain is BYO.
- `docs/USER_GUIDE.md:848-850`, `1001-1003` — for the llama.cpp walkthrough, states the user needs the vendor `LINUX_TOOLCHAIN`, a llama.cpp checkout, and the GGUF model.
- `Dockerfile.runtime:27-34` — states QEMU and vsim are **not** built into the image and must be volume-mounted at run time, with example `-v`/`-e` invocations. This is the most explicit "you provide these" text in the repo, and it lives in a Dockerfile comment.

What is missing:
- No "what's in the box" / "what you must obtain" section anywhere user-facing.
- No version or ABI compatibility matrix (which QEMU fork/tag? which vsim ABI pin? `docs/hybrid_state_transport_problems.md:343-345` references an "ABI v6 pin" that no user doc explains).
- The only formal delivery manifest is `docs/MRD.md:42-59` (the "What the customer buys" / "What the customer does NOT get" table) — **an internal PM document that must not ship**, and which describes a hypothetical future installer (`hsim` CLI, license daemon, encrypted vsim binary), not the current package.
- `docs/FRS.md:484-534` (FR-701..FR-705) specifies the installer, dependency declaration, uninstaller, and doc set as **requirements that do not yet exist**.

## 5. Supported engines/models and how the user picks one

**Yes — this is the best-covered area of the documentation.**

- `docs/USER_GUIDE.md:38-74` (§2) — the canonical answer. Shows `./andesim doctor`, `./andesim list models`, `./andesim list engines`, with a real sample table (`:52-58`: `qemu64`, `qemu32`, `vsim:ax45mpv_premium`, `vsim:ax46mpv_advanced` with TYPE/KIND/XLEN/VLEN/DLEN/ELEN columns), explains that engines are discovered by scanning `VSIM_BIN_DIR` for `sim_*` and probing `--describe`, and that `--engine` is optional when exactly one cycle engine is installed.
- `docs/USER_GUIDE.md:17-34` (§1) — the three models (`fast` / `cycle` / `hybrid`) in a comparison table.
- `docs/USER_GUIDE.md:266-306` (§5.1, §5.2) — full `--mode` and `--engine` reference, including auto-selection rules, the multi-engine disambiguation error text, rv32/rv64 width-mismatch rejection, hybrid's rv64-only requirement, and per-engine fixed VLEN (128–1024 supported in hybrid).
- `docs/USER_GUIDE.md:804-805` — troubleshooting rows for both engine-selection errors.
- `docs/engine_interface.md:140-171` — the discovery algorithm and how to add an engine.
- `driver/cmd_list.cpp` implements `list models|engines|fixtures`; `driver/main.cpp:58-62` marks `fixtures` dev-only (gated by `ANDESIM_DEV`), and `tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_release_surface.sh:36-45` contract-tests that `models` and `engines` appear in `--help` while `fixtures` does not.

Two caveats:
1. **No list of what engines actually ship.** The doc explains *how to enumerate* engines but never says which engines a customer receives. The example engine IDs (`ax45mpv_premium`, `ax46mpv_advanced`, `ax66_makatau`, `ax46mpv_fpga_l3`) appear scattered across `USER_GUIDE.md:56-57, 440`, `docs/llama_roi_howto.md:11-22`, `docs/engine_interface.md:6-7` — a user cannot tell which are real products, which are internal, and which their package includes. `REFACTOR_ROADMAP.md:6` mentions "all 4 rv64 vsim engines".
2. The whole flow presumes `VSIM_BIN_DIR` is already correctly populated, which loops back to gap G4.
